## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:specify` can materialize a spec whose own `## Current State` / `## Technical
Approach` section correctly identifies the affected component as living outside the plugin (a
third-party dependency, or in this case the Claude Code harness itself) — and still carry a
Deliverable/Acceptance-Criterion directing `/claude-tweaks:feedback` to file an upstream report
against that component. `feedback/SKILL.md`'s own scope line is explicit: "Do not use this skill
to file against any repository other than `thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks`." — and
`learning-routing.md`'s classifier would route a genuine harness/dependency quirk with no owning
claude-tweaks artifact to D4 (memory) or D2 (project doc), never D5, since D5 requires the learning
to name a `/claude-tweaks:*` skill, a `skills/_shared/*` contract, or a `bin/*.js` behavior. A spec
that both correctly diagnoses "this is not ours" and then asks for a `/claude-tweaks:feedback`
filing anyway is internally contradictory.

Reproduced by #1785 (materialized 2026-09-14): its `## Current State` explicitly corrects the
originally-filed attribution ("The record as filed attributes the guard to
`bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`. That attribution is wrong ... this is harness behavior"), yet its
Deliverables still directed: "File one upstream report through `/claude-tweaks:feedback` targeting
the Claude Code harness." That deliverable is structurally unreachable — `/claude-tweaks:feedback`
Step 2 would itself stop ("If it is not D5, stop") before ever reaching Step 3's self-reference
check. The build's own SDD fix-loop noticed the filing couldn't happen but reasoned it via an
inapplicable self-reference collapse (which only fires for a learning that already reached D5)
rather than catching that the learning never qualified as D5 in the first place.

## Deliverables

- Add a check to `/claude-tweaks:specify`'s spec-composition step (wherever a "Suggested change"
  from an `## Original request` becomes a Deliverable naming `/claude-tweaks:feedback`): before
  emitting a feedback-filing Deliverable, run the same classification `learning-routing.md`'s
  classifier and `feedback/SKILL.md` Step 2 would apply — does the record's own Current State /
  affected-component analysis place the subject inside the plugin (a `/claude-tweaks:*` skill,
  `skills/_shared/*` contract, or `bin/*.js` behavior)? If not, never emit the feedback-filing
  Deliverable/AC.
- When the check fails, route the spec's language instead per `learning-routing.md`'s own
  Non-claude-tweaks-upstream paragraph ("Report it to the user, name the owner, and stop") or its
  D4/D2 outcome — whichever this repo's spec-authoring convention should surface as — rather than
  silently omitting the concern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A spec whose Current State / Technical Approach already identifies the affected component as
  outside the plugin (third-party harness, dependency, or corrected mis-attribution) never carries
  a Deliverable or Acceptance Criterion directing `/claude-tweaks:feedback` to file against that
  component.
- `/claude-tweaks:specify`'s own spec-shape validation (or a `/claude-tweaks:challenge` lens) catches
  this class of solution-baked, unfileable deliverable before the spec reaches `ready`.
- Regression case: re-run `/claude-tweaks:specify` against a record shaped like #1785 (an originally
  mis-attributed harness quirk, corrected in the same spec) and confirm no feedback-filing
  Deliverable is emitted.

manifesto log line at all. When this second call resumed the same run directory for
`review,polish,wrap-up`, `config.yml` was missing entirely (confirmed via `ls`/`test -f`), forcing

(#2230/#2354/#2355, archived run `2026-09-13T224009-record-2230-2354-2355`) rather than reading
them back from the run's own first-call Manifesto write.

- Investigate why Step 3 did not execute (or executed but failed to persist `config.yml`) on a

## Acceptance Criteria

      levers by the time the call returns.

      record closes with that reasoning documented instead of a code change.

`decisions.md`'s `## /build`/`## /test` sections (real entries, no manifesto line) versus
`config.yml` absent from the run directory at the start of this second `/flow ... review,polish,wrap-up`
call; `test -f "$RUN_DIR/config.yml"` → `MISSING`, confirmed before this call wrote one itself.

## Cost this session

~10 minutes: reading manifesto.md's full lever-computation procedure, finding and cross-checking
the sibling bundle's archived config.yml as a same-day precedent, and manually composing +
writing the batch `set-config.js` call, instead of the value being readable off the run's own
first-call state.

AUTO 09:36:46 — manifesto: config.yml was missing on resume (this call's step list is
review,polish,wrap-up — the first call's build/test steps ran without ever writing it); wrote it
now, folding values from the sibling reconcile-residue bundle run (#2230,#2354,#2355, archived
2026-09-14T01:01, same policy.yml/autonomy=unattended, merged via PR #2387)...

The dispatched `/claude-tweaks:flow #1841 build,test` Task call safely stopped at Step 2.8's claim-contest check (the record's live claim, held by a different, non-expired run, correctly blocked a second claim) and deduplicated against an existing self-report (#2394) from an earlier firing that hit the identical contest ~2 hours prior. Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `resolveRecords` ladder has three rungs: (a) the run dir's own
`work/*-spec.md` headers, (b) the worktree's mirror of that same run dir (via `worktreeMirror`),
and (c) a parent multi-spec run's `manifest.yml` ids plus any `spec-*/work/` headers found by
`deps.readdir(runDir)`. Only rungs (a) and (b) apply worktree-mirroring; rung (c) reads `spec-*`
subdirectories directly from `runDir` (the main-checkout path `--run` anchors to), never from the
worktree.

For a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` file-overlap group (2+ records sharing one worktree/branch/PR),
`materialize.md` writes each record's header to `{run-dir}/spec-{n}/work/{n}-spec.md` and commits
it on the feature branch -- so on a real pr-first run it exists only inside the worktree's own
working tree, never in the main-checkout run dir, exactly the same reason rungs (a)/(b) already
mirror. Observed live on run `2026-09-14T000308-record-2283-2338` (group #2283,#2338):
`node bin/wrap-up-pack.js --run "$RUN_DIR"` returned `recordLabels`, `claim`, `ledger`, and
`unblocked` all as `{ok: false, error: "records unresolved -- no materialized header or manifest
found"}` even though both `spec-2283/work/2283-spec.md` and `spec-2338/work/2338-spec.md` existed
and were readable inside the worktree.

## Deliverables

Extend rung (c) in `resolveRecords` (`bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`) to also check
`worktreeMirror(runDir, worktree)` for `spec-*/work/` headers and the mirrored `manifest.yml`,
the same way rung (b) mirrors rung (a) -- falling back to the existing `runDir`-only read when no
worktree resolves or the mirror has nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture reproducing this run's shape (main-checkout run dir with no `work/` or `spec-*/`
  entries; a separate worktree dir carrying `spec-{n}/work/{n}-spec.md` for 2+ records) resolves

- The four probes that depend on `resolveRecords` (`recordLabels`, `claim`, `ledger`, `unblocked`)
  succeed against that fixture instead of returning `records unresolved`.
- Existing `resolveRecords`/`wrap-up-pack` tests continue to pass unchanged.

Mirror rung (b)'s existing pattern (`worktreeMirror(runDir, worktree)`) into rung (c): when the
direct `runDir`-anchored `spec-*/work/` read finds nothing, resolve the worktree mirror path the
same helper rung (b) already uses, and re-run the same `spec-*/work/` + `manifest.yml` read
against that mirrored path before falling back to `unavailable`. No new mirroring mechanism --
reuse the existing `worktreeMirror` helper rungs (a)/(b) already call.

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` -- `resolveRecords`'s rung (c), and the `worktreeMirror` helper

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2422 (same hardcoded-`main`-vs-integration-branch-ladder theme, different file)

## Current State

`bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `resolveHeader` (the function backing `bin/wrap-up-pack.js`'s
`residue`, `state`, and `blastRadius` probes) resolves the integration branch at line 233-238:

```js
const policy = {
  integrationBranch: values['integration-branch'] || '',
  ...
};
const integrationBranch = policy.integrationBranch || 'main';
sources.integrationBranch = policy.integrationBranch ? 'policy' : 'default';
```

It only ever consults `resolvePolicy`'s `integration-branch` key. When that key is unset (no
`.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` pin), it falls straight to the literal string `'main'` -- never
consulting `skills/_shared/integration-branch.md`'s canonical ladder (routine template ->
policy.yml -> CLAUDE.md prose -> git/`gh repo view` default -> per-consumer fallback), which
exists precisely so callers don't each hardcode their own guess.

On a repository whose actual default branch is not `main` (e.g. `master`), with no
`integration-branch:` policy key set, this causes `residue`/`state`/`blastRadius` to fail:
`could not resolve merge base of "main" and HEAD"` (`blastRadius`) or `"base unresolved -- no
merge-base against the integration branch"` (`residue`/`state`). `sources.integrationBranch`
then reports `"default"` -- i.e. the pack's own provenance trace correctly shows it never
consulted policy.yml, CLAUDE.md, or git/gh at all.

`skills/wrap-up/residue-sweep.md` already documents the correct pattern for a sibling caller:
"`--integration-branch` must always be passed explicitly -- never rely on the CLI's own
default... resolve `{ref}` via `skills/_shared/integration-branch.md`'s canonical ladder before
invoking the CLI." `pack.js`'s `resolveHeader` is the one caller that still bypasses this.

## Deliverables

- `resolveHeader` in `bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` resolves `integrationBranch` via
  `skills/_shared/integration-branch.md`'s canonical ladder (minus the routine-template rank,
  which has no meaning inside this CLI -- policy.yml -> CLAUDE.md prose -> git/`gh repo view`
  default), not a bare `policy.integrationBranch || 'main'` fallback.
- `sources.integrationBranch` reports which ladder rank actually resolved the value (e.g.
  `'policy'`, `'git-default'`), not just the binary `'policy'`/`'default'` it reports today --
  so a reader of the pack's own provenance trace can tell which rank fired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a repository whose actual default branch is not `main`, with no `integration-branch:` key
  in `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`, running `node bin/wrap-up-pack.js --run <run-dir>` resolves the
  real default branch (via git/`gh repo view`) instead of hardcoding `main`, and the
  `residue`/`state`/`blastRadius` probes run to completion instead of failing on an unresolved
  merge base.
- `inputs.sources.integrationBranch` in the pack's output reflects the actual resolution source,
  never silently reporting `'default'` when a real ladder rank (git/gh, or CLAUDE.md prose) fired.
- A repository that already sets `integration-branch:` in `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml` is
  unaffected -- this fix only changes what happens when that key is absent.
- Existing tests covering `pack.js`'s header resolution still pass; add a test covering the
  non-`main`-default, no-policy-key case this record reports.

## Technical Approach

Replace `pack.js`'s bare `policy.integrationBranch || 'main'` fallback with a call into
`skills/_shared/integration-branch.md`'s canonical resolution -- the same git/`gh repo view`
default-branch lookup `residue-sweep.md` already instructs its own callers to perform before
invoking `bin/residue.js` directly. Reuse whatever resolver function backs that lookup elsewhere
in `bin/lib/` (check for an existing `resolveIntegrationBranch`-shaped helper before writing a
new one -- `bin/lib/reconcile/` and `bin/resolve-policy.js` both touch this same ladder and may
already export a reusable piece). Thread the resolved value's source rank through to
`sources.integrationBranch` so the pack's own provenance trace stays accurate.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` -- `resolveHeader`'s integration-branch fallback (line ~233-238)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/integration-branch.md` -- the canonical ladder this fix must follow, not restate
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/residue-sweep.md` -- the existing sibling-caller pattern to mirror

## Gotchas

- Workaround used to file this record: invoking `bin/residue.js` and `bin/blast-radius.js`
  directly with an explicit `--base`/`--integration-branch master`, bypassing `pack.js`'s own
  (broken) resolution for those two fields -- confirms the underlying probes work correctly once
  given the right branch name; the defect is isolated to `pack.js`'s own resolution step.
- `merge-size-probe.js`, `release/precheck.js`, and `release-preflight/pack.js` carry similar
  `|| 'main'` fallbacks (found via a repo-wide grep while shaping this record) -- out of scope
  for this record, which is filed specifically against `wrap-up-pack.js`'s probes; worth a
  follow-up capture if they prove to have the same defect.

## Original request

wrap-up-pack.js: residue/state/blastRadius probes hardcode "main" instead of the canonical integration-branch ladder

**Summary:** `bin/wrap-up-pack.js`'s `residue`, `state`, and `blastRadius` probes all failed on a repository whose default branch is not literally named `main`, with `could not resolve merge base of "main" and HEAD`. `skills/_shared/integration-branch.md` documents a canonical resolution ladder (explicit arg -> routine template -> `policy.yml`'s `integration-branch:` key -> CLAUDE.md prose -> git/`gh repo view` default -> per-consumer fallback) specifically so callers don't each hardcode their own guess, but this tool's `main` fallback bypasses that ladder entirely.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/wrap-up-pack.js`

**Repro steps:**
1. In a repository whose actual default branch is `master` (not `main`), with no `integration-branch:` key set in `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`.
2. Run `node bin/wrap-up-pack.js --run <a valid pipeline run dir>`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the tool resolves the integration branch via `_shared/integration-branch.md`'s ladder (landing on the repo's actual default via `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef` / `git remote show origin`) and the `residue`/`state`/`blastRadius` probes run normally.
Actual: all three probes fail with `error: "could not resolve merge base of \"main\" and HEAD"` (`blastRadius`) or `"base unresolved -- no merge-base against the integration branch"` (`residue`/`state`), and the pack's own `inputs.sources.integrationBranch` reports `"default"` -- i.e. it never consulted policy.yml, CLAUDE.md, or git/gh at all.

**Definition:** Clear -- cite `_shared/integration-branch.md` in `wrap-up-pack.js` the same way `residue-sweep.md` already instructs its own caller to resolve `{ref}` before invoking `bin/residue.js` directly. Workaround used this run: invoke `bin/residue.js` and `bin/blast-radius.js` directly with an explicit `--base`/`--integration-branch master`, bypassing the pack's own (broken) resolution for those fields.

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#1985 (unmerged, PR #2298) adds a "Drain-overlap hold" to `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`'s Auto-merge gate: before Authorization/Content judgment, `drain-pr-overlap.md`'s Step 6 checks whether this group's PR overlaps a still-open PR opened earlier by the same drain firing, and if so, explicitly **skips Authorization and Content judgment** and "fall[s] back to the normal Review Console for this group," logging:

```
AUTO {time} — Auto-merge gate: group [{issues}] held — overlaps drain PR #{pr} on {files}; merge order is a human call. Reversibility: n/a.
```

Separately, `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js`'s `needsHumanVerdict()` (the ONLY mechanism `mergeResolution()` consults to decide `leave-open` before falling through to a plain grant check) is:

```js
function needsHumanVerdict(decisions) {
  return decisionLines(decisions).find((l) => /needs-human/i.test(l) && /merge-check|assess-agent-autonomy/i.test(l)) || null;
}
```

This regex requires BOTH `needs-human` AND (`merge-check`|`assess-agent-autonomy`) on the same `decisions.md` line — a signal that only ever comes from `assess-agent-autonomy`'s Content-judgment Layer 2 (`settle-and-merge.md`, around the `2. **Content judgment**` step). Because the drain-overlap hold explicitly *skips* Content judgment, no such verdict is ever computed or logged for a drain-held group. `mergeResolution()` therefore finds no needs-human verdict, falls through to its grant check, and if every group member carries `auto:merge` or a matured `auto:merge-pending`, returns `{resolution: 'merge', reason: 'every member carries auto:merge...'}`.

Traced (not yet reproduced live): under `autonomy: unattended`, `wrap-up/review-console.md`'s Auto-resolution short-circuit invokes exactly this `console-resolve.js` merge resolution with zero human interaction. A group held back by the #1985 drain-overlap hold would reach the Review Console, and — because the hold produces no signal `needsHumanVerdict()` recognizes — the unattended auto-resolver would compute `resolution: 'merge'` and merge it anyway, silently defeating the entire purpose of the #1985 hold for exactly the operating mode (`unattended`) most likely to run a multi-group drain unattended. This is one layer downstream of the original #1480/#1596 incident #1985 was filed to prevent.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Give `console-resolve.js`'s merge-resolution path a way to recognize a live drain-overlap hold and resolve to `leave-open` for it, analogous to the existing `needs-human` carve-out — but the semantics differ: the existing carve-out (`assess-agent-autonomy` verdict) is treated as **permanent** ("authoritative all the way down," per `settle-and-merge.md`), while `drain-pr-overlap.md`'s own Step 6 hold is explicitly **not** persisted — it re-reads the overlapping PR's current state every time it runs and self-heals once that PR merges/closes. A naive regex addition that treats any historical "held — overlaps drain PR" decisions.md line as permanent would make the unattended resolver *more* conservative than #1985's own design intends. The real fix likely needs `console-resolve.js` to re-run (or receive as an already-fresh input) the same `detectCrossPRFileOverlap` check drain-pr-overlap.md's Step 6 performs, rather than trusting a historical log line — design thought needed on where that fresh state comes from at console-resolve time (a fact-pack field? a re-invocation of the check inline in resolve.js?).
- [ ] Tests: a fixture where a group's decisions.md carries a "held — overlaps drain PR" line and the overlapping PR is still open -> `mergeResolution` returns `leave-open`; the same fixture with the overlapping PR now merged/closed -> returns `merge` (assuming grants otherwise satisfy).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Under `autonomy: unattended`, a group held by #1985's drain-overlap hold is never auto-merged by `console-resolve.js` while the overlapping drain PR is still open, even when every member otherwise carries `auto:merge`.
2. Once the overlapping drain PR merges or closes, the same group's next Review Console evaluation resolves normally (no permanent lockout).
3. `npm test` green; existing `tests/bin-lib/console/resolve.test.js` cases unaffected.

## Technical Approach

Needs design thought (hence deferred): the cleanest shape is probably a new field in the run's fact pack (or `console.json`) that records the *live* drain-overlap state at Review-Console-render time, since the console's own render already runs after the Auto-merge gate would have logged the hold — the resolver could read that field instead of re-deriving from decisions.md text. Alternatively, a literal-but-honest log-line addition (e.g. `drain-overlap-hold: live` vs `drain-overlap-hold: resolved`) that `console-resolve.js` re-validates against current PR state before trusting.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — `needsHumanVerdict()`/`mergeResolution()`
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/drain-pr-overlap.md` — Step 6, the hold's own log line
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — Auto-resolution short-circuit's carve-out list
- `tests/bin-lib/console/resolve.test.js`

## Gotchas

- Do not just make the hold's log line match the existing `needs-human`+`merge-check` regex — that would be dishonest (it isn't an `assess-agent-autonomy` verdict) and would inherit the "permanent" semantics that don't fit this hold's self-healing design.
- This gap does not affect #1944/#1984/#1985's own PR #2298 (none of the three carry `auto:merge`, so this run's own merge decision never reaches `mergeResolution()`'s grant-check branch) — it only affects a *future* group that both carries `auto:merge` and gets caught by the #1985 hold in a live unattended drain.

## Original request

Found during `/claude-tweaks:review` of #1944/#1984/#1985 (dispatch pre-build safety checks bundle, PR #2298) — self-referential review of dispatch's own merge-gating machinery surfaced this cross-cutting gap between #1985's new hold and the pre-existing unattended console auto-resolver.

**Related:** #1944, #1984, #1985

Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js`'s `readMembers` (the `unattended` Review Console resolver behind `bin/console-resolve.js`, #1932) takes the member list from `wrap-up-pack.json`'s `inputs.records` when a pack exists, else scans `{runDir}/work/*-spec.md` headers only. `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `resolveRecords` is the producer of that same list and climbs a three-rung ladder: the run dir's own `work/` headers, the worktree's mirror of the run dir (`worktreeMirror`), then a parent multi-spec run's `manifest.yml` ids plus every `spec-*/work/` header (`source: 'manifest'`). `resolveRecords` and `headerRecords` are module-private — `pack.js` exports only `gatherPack`, `resolveInputs`, `wrapProbe`, `parseLedger`, `PROBE_NAMES` — so `readMembers` carries a hand-copied first rung and nothing else.

Consequence: against a multi-spec parent run dir (headers under `spec-{a}/work/`, `spec-{b}/work/`) at any point where `wrap-up-pack.json` is absent or unparseable, `readMembers` returns `[]`, `readSnapshot` skips `readGrants`, and `resolveAll` resolves the merge half to `leave-open` with reason `members-unresolved` even when every member carries `auto:merge`. The single-spec fallback (`{runDir}/work/`) works today and must keep working byte-for-byte.

Both modules read through the same `deps` shape (`readFile`, `readdir` — `console-resolve.js` wires `fs.readFileSync`/`fs.readdirSync` with a catch-to-`[]` readdir, identical to `pack.js`'s default deps), so the ladder can be shared rather than copied a second time.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` exports `resolveRecords` (and `headerRecords`) alongside the existing exports; no behavior change inside `pack.js`.
- [ ] `readMembers` in `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` replaces its inline `work/` scan with a call to `resolveRecords(deps, runDir, worktree)` and returns its `records`, keeping the pack-first branch (`inputs.records` wins whenever it is non-empty) unchanged.
- [ ] The worktree argument for the second rung comes from `{runDir}/run-state.json`'s `worktree` string when present (read via the existing `readJson`), else `null` — and `worktreeMirror` in `pack.js` returns `null` for a non-string worktree instead of throwing from `path.join`, so the console path with no run-state file degrades to rungs one and three.
- [ ] Regression tests in `tests/bin-lib/console/resolve.test.js` using its existing `fixture` helper (extend it with `manifest`/`specHeaders` options): (a) a multi-spec parent run dir with no `wrap-up-pack.json`, `manifest.yml` listing two spec ids and headers under `spec-*/work/`, resolves `members` to those ids and no longer yields `members-unresolved`; (b) the existing single-spec header case and the pack-wins case stay green unchanged.
- [ ] One export-shape assertion in `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` (or its conformance sibling) that `resolveRecords` is exported and still reports `source: 'manifest'` for the parent-run fixture, so the shared ladder cannot silently regress to private again.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. With no `wrap-up-pack.json` and members only under `spec-*/work/` (plus `manifest.yml` ids), `readSnapshot(...).members` equals the sorted unique union `resolveRecords` reports for the same run dir.
2. With no pack and headers under `{runDir}/work/` only, `members` is byte-identical to today's output (same order, same de-duplication, `record:` frontmatter still wins over the filename).
3. With a non-empty `inputs.records` in the pack, `members` is taken from the pack and the ladder is never consulted.
4. `resolve.js` contains no second copy of the header-scanning regex after the change; `pack.js`'s `resolveRecords` is the only implementation of the ladder.
5. `readMembers` never throws on a run dir with no `run-state.json` or a `run-state.json` without a `worktree` string.
6. `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Export, don't copy: the drift exists because the first rung was transcribed into `resolve.js`; adding the third rung by transcription would leave the second rung (worktree mirror, #1930 review C1) missing and set up the next drift. `resolveRecords` already returns `{ records, source }`; `readMembers` keeps its pack-first branch and delegates the fallback:

```js
const state = readJson(deps, path.join(runDir, 'run-state.json'));
const worktree = state && typeof state.worktree === 'string' ? state.worktree : null;
return resolveRecords(deps, runDir, worktree).records;
```

`pack.js` requires `../flow/manifest` for `parseManifestYaml` already; `resolve.js` requiring `../wrap-up/pack` is a one-way dependency (pack.js does not import the console module), so no cycle.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — `readMembers` (fallback scan to replace), `readJson`/`readText` helpers, `readSnapshot` (the `members.length` guard around `readGrants`).
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `headerRecords`, `worktreeMirror`, `resolveRecords`, `module.exports` line.
- `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js` — `resolverDeps` wiring (`readFile`, `readdir`); no change expected.
- `tests/bin-lib/console/resolve.test.js` — fixture helper writes `wrap-up-pack.json` and `work/{n}-spec.md`; extend for `manifest.yml` + `spec-*/work/`.
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` — the `resolveInputs (c)` parent multi-spec case (#1930 review C1) is the ladder's existing coverage; add the export assertion beside it.

## Gotchas
- `worktreeMirror(runDir, null)` throws today (`path.join` on `null`), but only `resolveRecords` calls it and today's sole caller always passes a string; the null-guard is what makes the console path safe, so it is part of this change, not an optional nicety.
- `readMembers` deliberately ignores the pack when `inputs.records` is empty (`fromPack.length` check) — keep that: an empty pack list falls through to the ladder, as before.
- `pack.js`'s `readText` and `resolve.js`'s `readText` are byte-identical helpers; do not try to share them — the deps object is what is shared, and each module's helper stays with it.
- `manifest.yml` is parsed with `parseManifestYaml` from `bin/lib/flow/manifest.js`; the fixture needs a `multispec.specs[].id` shape, not a flat list.

## Original request
Found by the pre-v6.119.0 whole-branch review (range e7d6d9331..4db32e020): a producer/consumer drift between wrap-up/pack.js's record-discovery and console-resolve.js's own fallback copy.

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `acceptance-labeling` check (registered via `registerCheck('acceptance-labeling', ...)`) unconditionally expects a resolved, non-parent-linked issue to carry `demo:pending` plus a Confirmed comment/brief, rendering `fail` when it's absent. `wrap-up/verification-brief.md`'s Oversight-floor gate (`#367`, `bin/lib/issues/oversight-floor.js`'s `exceedsOversightFloor`) legitimately skips Steps 1-4 (no `demo:pending` bootstrap, no brief) for a record whose `risk`/`size` facets don't clear the project's configured `risk-floor`/`size-floor` — e.g. a `risk:low`/`size:low` record under a run resolving `risk-floor: high`/`size-floor: high`. `engine-verify.js` has no knowledge of this exemption, so `wrap-up-engine.js verify` renders `acceptance-labeling` as `fail` and exits 3 for every such record, withholding the closure line even though the record's labeling is exactly as `verification-brief.md` intends.

Observed live during #1841's own wrap-up: the record carries `risk:low`/`size:low`, the resolved run policy set `risk-floor: high`/`size-floor: high`, `exceedsOversightFloor` correctly returned `exceeds: false`, Steps 1-4 were correctly skipped — and `verify`'s `acceptance-labeling` row then rendered `fail — #1841: missing demo:pending label`, a false negative on a check that was never supposed to run for this record.

## Deliverables

- `acceptance-labeling`'s check needs a way to know a record was Oversight-floor-exempted, so it can render `skip (oversight floor not cleared)` instead of `fail` for that record — likely by having `verification-brief.md`'s Oversight-floor gate write the outcome into `verify-expectations.json` (a new field, e.g. `oversightExempt: [n1, n2]`) the same way `memory`/`upstream` are already written there, and having `engine-verify.js` read it before checking for `demo:pending`.
- Extend `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js`: an issue listed in `verify-expectations.json`'s new exemption field renders `acceptance-labeling` as `skip`, never `fail`, even with no `demo:pending` label present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record whose Oversight-floor gate resolved `exceeds: false` (recorded in `verify-expectations.json`) renders `acceptance-labeling` as `skip`, and does not trip `verify`'s exit-3 gate on that account alone.
- A record that genuinely should carry `demo:pending` but doesn't still renders `fail` as today — the fix narrows the false-positive population, it does not loosen the check generally.
- `npm test` passes.

Origin: /claude-tweaks:feedback session-evaluation (self-assessment, degraded from a failed Frontier judge dispatch), self-referential run (this repo's own origin is thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks) — routed to a normal backlog record per Step 3 rather than filed as upstream feedback.

## Current State

`node plugin/bin/release.js <minor|patch> "<summary>" --dry-run` (and the live invocation) emits roughly 490 lines of `fatal: path '<path>' exists on disk, but not in '<sha>'` git stderr noise while walking history to locate the last version-bump commit, before reaching its actual result. In one observed run, 492 of 497 total output lines were this noise; only the final ~5 lines (`[dry-run] would bump ...`) were the actual answer, forcing the output to be redirected to a file and tailed rather than read directly.

## Deliverables

Either suppress/redirect the walk's expected-to-fail probe commands' stderr internally in `plugin/bin/lib/release/` (the history-walk implementation), or stop the walk as soon as a version-bump commit is found rather than continuing all the way to the repo root.

Origin: /claude-tweaks:feedback session-evaluation (self-assessment, degraded from a failed Frontier judge dispatch), self-referential run (this repo's own origin is thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks) — routed to a normal backlog record per Step 3 rather than filed as upstream feedback.

## Current State

Worktrees created via the harness-native `EnterWorktree` tool (rather than `plugin/skills/dispatch/`'s own `record-worktree` CLI) never get their worktree/branch association written into that run's `run-state.json`. Downstream, `teardown-run`/`archive-run` (`plugin/bin/hooks.js`) can't find the association and report "no worktree recorded" instead of tearing the worktree down automatically. In one session this recurred across 7 separate worktrees, each requiring a manual `git merge-base --is-ancestor` proof + `git worktree remove --force` + `git branch -D` + `gh api -X DELETE .../refs/heads/{branch}` sequence in place of one CLI call — roughly 14 extra manual commands that a working association would have made unnecessary. A related recovery-quality symptom from the same gap: a prior session's main checkout was found 256 commits behind `origin/main` while still holding uncommitted archival bookkeeping from an earlier `/tidy` run — state left behind with no automatic reconciliation path, blocking a later session's own `archive-run` calls until manually resolved via a scratch-worktree PR.

Related, narrower observation from the same evaluation: the ledger's canonical Create location (`docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}-ledger.md`, per `_shared/ledger-format.md`) requires a worktree write under `worktree-always`, but `residue-sweep.md` explicitly expects a standalone (no-worktree) wrap-up run to be able to create one "so the ledger's own resolve gate has something to enforce on a standalone run." In practice a standalone run has no lightweight path to satisfy this — creating a ledger file for a single non-blocking item means a full worktree-commit-push-PR-merge cycle for a file that gets deleted moments later once resolved.

## Deliverables

1. Either make `EnterWorktree` call `record-worktree` itself when the harness detects a claude-tweaks-managed repo, or make `teardown-run`/`archive-run` fall back to `git worktree list`/branch-name matching when `run-state.json` carries no worktree field.
2. Let a standalone, no-worktree wrap-up log ledger items to a location that doesn't require a worktree write — e.g. `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/` (already commit-exempt under `worktree-always` and already the run's own audit-trail home) instead of `docs/plans/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree entered via `EnterWorktree` during a dispatch/wrap-up run is torn down by `teardown-run`/`archive-run` without a "no worktree recorded" failure and without any manual `git worktree remove`/`git branch -D`/`gh api DELETE` fallback.
- A standalone wrap-up run with at least one ledger item can create, resolve, and delete its ledger without needing a worktree, a commit, or a PR.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review. Two independently-merged PRs each shipped their
own Jaccard-similarity tokenizer and threshold constant, with no shared source and no test
importing either exported constant — so a change to one can silently invalidate the other's
tests without either noticing:

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` (confirmed, line 17, #1980): `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN = 0.4`
  + `SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS` (line 22).
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` (confirmed, line 24, #1944):
  `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.5` + `STOP_WORDS` (line 30).

A search of `tests/` for either constant name returns zero hits —
`tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js:66` hardcodes "0.5" in a test name/reasoning
(`'title similarity below the default 0.5 threshold does not fire'`) instead of importing the
real constant.

## Deliverables

- Decide whether these two similarity checks are conceptually the same primitive (in which case
  consolidate into one shared tokenizer/threshold module both import) or genuinely distinct
  enough to justify separate constants (in which case document why, and have each test import
  its own module's real constant instead of hardcoding the value).
- Update `near-duplicate.test.js` to import `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` rather than
  hardcoding 0.5.

## Acceptance Criteria

No test hardcodes either threshold as a bare numeric literal; both are imported from their
source module.

## Technical Approach

Read both modules' full similarity-scoring logic (`coordination.js`'s substance-similarity check
and `near-duplicate.js`'s title-similarity check) to judge whether they're the same primitive
applied to different inputs (substance text vs. titles) or genuinely distinct enough to warrant
separate stop-word lists and thresholds — this is the actual judgment call the Deliverables ask
for, not a mechanical decision this shaping pass can make without reading both algorithms'
full bodies. If consolidating: extract a shared tokenizer/stop-word/threshold module both import,
preserving each call site's own threshold value unless the investigation finds a reason to unify
those too. If keeping them separate: add a one-line comment at each constant's definition site
stating why the two are conceptually distinct, and fix the test regardless — the test-hardcoding
fix (Deliverable 2) applies either way. Update `near-duplicate.test.js:66` to import
`DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` and interpolate it into the test name/assertion instead of
the bare literal `0.5`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` — `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN`/`SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS`, possible

  possible consolidation target
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js` (line 66) — fix the hardcoded `0.5`

- Per a standing memory in this codebase, similarity scores are normalization-sensitive —
  consolidating the two tokenizers is only safe if their actual normalization behavior (case
  folding, punctuation handling, stop-word removal order) genuinely matches; verify with a
  substitution+diff test before assuming they're interchangeable, not just by reading the
  constant values.

  score computed by a merged tokenizer can differ from the original even at the "same" nominal
  threshold value if the tokenization itself changes; re-verify both modules' existing test

Surface: infra

## Current State

Reconcile's automated hygiene sweep flags this pipeline run directory as `structurally-stuck` (`reason: no-branch`) for many consecutive passes — the cache entry for this path (`.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json`, `structurally-stuck:{path}`) shows `count: 42`, `lastError: "stuck at no-branch"`, `escalated: true` — auto-filing this issue per `bin/lib/reconcile`'s escalation mechanism (#644 Deliverable 2 / #1613's visibility layer).

The stuck directory: `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-08-26T155419-record-1413`. Its `run-state.json` **does** stamp `worktree: .claude/worktrees/dispatch-record-1413` (unlike #2228/#2230's `no-worktree` instances) and `pr: {number: 1497, url: ...}` (no `pr.branch` field). Issue #1413 is closed; `decisions.md` records the actual disposition: the record's own deliverable turned out to already be implemented and merged elsewhere (commit `0ae01b6d6`, refs #989) before this run's worktree ever branched — "a stale duplicate of an already-closed gap, not a live defect. No code change made." PR #1497 was closed without merging as a result.

**This does not match #2226's or #2228's diagnosed root causes**, and the mismatch is itself the finding worth recording: empirically re-running the exact functions `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` uses against this repo's *current* live state gives a different picture than the escalation cache's sticky `lastError`:
- `resolvePrStateByNumber(root, 1497)` (from `bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js`) returns `{state: 'CLOSED', mergedAt: null, mergeCommit: null, ...}` right now — the by-number probe's `CLOSED` branch (the one #2226 found is missing a `MERGED` case) *should* be reachable and *should* match here, since this PR really is `CLOSED`, not `MERGED`.
- This run directory carries no `console.json` at all (confirmed by directory listing), so `readConsoleState(dir)` returns `'none'` — which, per the current code, routes to `skipped.push({ reason: 'console-never-rendered' })` and **never calls `trackStuckSkip`** (the function that updates `reconcile-cache.json` and drives the 7-day/3-strike escalation). A skip landing there could never accumulate a `structurally-stuck` count for `no-branch` at all going forward.

So either (a) the escalation cache's `lastError` field is stale from earlier passes and this directory has, in fact, moved to a `console-never-rendered` skip more recently (in which case it's silently stuck in a *different*, currently-untracked bucket — `console-never-rendered` has no TTL/escalation of its own), or (b) something upstream of the by-number probe (the outer `if (!branch)` gate, or an intermediate `gh` failure) is preventing the probe from ever running on the actual pass(es) that produced these 42 counts, which this investigation did not fully pin down.

## Deliverables

- Investigate directly (re-run reconcile's real archive-merged pass — dry-run flag if available — against this repo, or add temporary tracing) to determine exactly which branch of `archive-merged.js`'s logic this run dir currently lands in, rather than trusting the escalation cache's `lastError`, which this investigation found reason to doubt.
- If the finding is "stuck at `console-never-rendered` with no escalation path": that reason is deliberately excluded from `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (per the code's own comment, "each already has its own clear resolution path... that doesn't need this generic staleness backstop") — but a run dir whose PR is closed-unmerged and whose console was simply never rendered (this run stopped early on a duplicate-detection assessment, never reaching a review console) has no such path today. Decide whether `console-never-rendered` needs its own resolution route for a closed-and-abandoned (never-merged) PR specifically, distinct from the in-flight case the current exclusion is written for.
- If the finding instead confirms a genuine gap in the by-number probe itself (e.g., the outer `if (!branch)` gate not being reached the way this investigation assumed), fix that gap and land a regression test pinning it.
- Once diagnosed and fixed, resolve this specific stuck directory (`2026-08-26T155419-record-1413`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The actual current skip reason for `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-08-26T155419-record-1413` is confirmed empirically (not assumed from the escalation cache alone).
- [ ] Whichever gap that reveals (a missing resolution path for `console-never-rendered` on a closed-unmerged PR, or a different bug in the by-number probe) is fixed, with a regression test.
- [ ] `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-08-26T155419-record-1413` is archived (or otherwise resolved) and no longer reported `structurally-stuck` by reconcile.
- [ ] The escalation cache's `lastError` staleness (if confirmed) is itself noted as a secondary finding — a `lastError` that doesn't reflect the branch a run dir currently lands in makes future triage of these auto-filed issues unreliable.

## Technical Approach

Start from `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s main sweep loop (~line 1270 onward: the `stampedWorktree`/`wtEntry`/`branch` derivation, the `#1962` by-number fallback block, `readConsoleState`, `decideArchive`) and trace this specific run dir through it step by step (or add a one-off diagnostic script that calls the same functions this investigation already called: `resolvePrStateByNumber`, `readConsoleState`, `fallbackBranch`) to find exactly where the current pass actually terminates. Cross-check against `.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json`'s own `residueFailures` structure (`bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js`) to see whether other `structurally-stuck` entries show the same live-vs-cached mismatch, which would point at a systemic staleness issue in `trackResidue`/`recordResidueFailure` rather than something specific to this one run dir.

### Key Files

- `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — the sweep loop and `#1962` fallback to trace/fix
- `bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` — `trackResidue`/`recordResidueFailure`, if the `lastError` staleness finding needs a fix here instead
- `bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js` — `fallbackBranch`/`branchExists`, read-only inputs to the diagnosis
- `tests/` (reconcile suite) — add the regression test for whichever gap is confirmed

## Gotchas

- This record's evidence does **not** support the same root cause as #2226 (MERGED-state gap) or #2228 (`stampedWorktree` gate gap) — do not assume either of those fixes resolves this directory without first confirming which branch this run dir actually lands in today.
- This directory has no `console.json` because the run stopped at an early duplicate-detection assessment and never reached a review console — a legitimately different lifecycle shape than a normal build-review-merge run, which may be exactly why the existing `console-never-rendered` exclusion doesn't fit it.
- The near-duplicate screen does not flag reconcile-residue records against each other by design (title-similarity excluded for `reconcile:`-prefixed titles) — the cross-references to #2226/#2228 above are a manual note, not an automated signal.
- `archiveRunDir`'s moves-first, close-last ordering must be preserved for whatever fix lands here.

## Current State

docs/plugin-structure.md's `_shared` row (lines 94 and 100) was amended by commit 399981c52 ("ceremony-profile.md rowed in plugin-structure", refs #1926) after a whole-branch review lens flagged its absence — the opposite outcome from the #1995 `dispatch-waiting.md` case this skill cites as its only worked example, so the skill's unconditional "needs nothing" claim no longer matches actual reviewed practice.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
- **A new `_shared/*.md` file registers in `docs/skill-graph.md` only — `docs/plugin-structure.md` needs nothing.** Step 3's "cross-reference `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s per-skill sub-file table as a registration site" is right for a skill's *own* lazy-loaded sub-file and wrong for a `_shared` contract: that doc carries one curated row for the whole directory (`plugin/skills/_shared/*.md → Cross-skill shared content … — see the directory listing`), not a per-file table, so adding a row there is drift, not registration. Step 4's edge is still owed, including when no skill names the new file directly — file the graph row under the section for the reader it addresses and say so in the row. #1995's `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` is the worked case: one `docs/skill-graph.md` row filed under `dispatch` ("cited only from the contract's one-line pointer — no skill names it directly … for want of a section for contract-owned files"), no `plugin-structure.md` edit, ruling narrowed from the plan's first draft at whole-branch review.
```

**Proposed:**
```
- **A new `_shared/*.md` file's `docs/skill-graph.md` edge is mandatory; a `docs/plugin-structure.md` mention is a judgment call, not a given.** Step 3's "cross-reference `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s per-skill sub-file table as a registration site" is right for a skill's *own* lazy-loaded sub-file and wrong to apply unmodified to a `_shared` contract: that doc carries one curated row for the whole directory (`plugin/skills/_shared/*.md → Cross-skill shared content … — see the directory listing`), not a per-file table, so adding a *new dedicated row* there is drift, not registration. Step 4's edge is still owed, including when no skill names the new file directly — file the graph row under the section for the reader it addresses and say so in the row. #1995's `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` is the worked case for staying out of `plugin-structure.md` entirely: one `docs/skill-graph.md` row filed under `dispatch` ("cited only from the contract's one-line pointer — no skill names it directly … for want of a section for contract-owned files"), no `plugin-structure.md` edit, ruling narrowed from the plan's first draft at whole-branch review. That is not the only outcome, though: #1926's `_shared/ceremony-profile.md` was added *into* the curated row itself on a review finding ("the curated `_shared` row lists ceremony-profile.md", `399981c52`) — the row's own self-description ("a curated subset … only the fragments worth calling out here") makes whether to fold the new file into that curated list an explicit judgment call each extraction has to make, not a rule that always resolves to "nothing."
```

## Acceptance Criteria

The Gotchas section's absolute claim that a new `_shared/*.md` file never needs a `docs/plugin-structure.md` mention is contradicted by #1926's `_shared/ceremony-profile.md`, which a whole-branch review explicitly required adding to that doc's curated `_shared` row.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `archiveRunDir` no longer renames a run directory whole — #1713/#1714 made the gitignored half move entry-by-entry and the per-spec loop skip whole `spec-{n}/` renames, and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` pins the `ENOTEMPTY` case. The split state this record describes still wedges, one level down. Live evidence at 2026-09-09: `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-08-29T153740-spec-1296-1336/` holds only the two git-tracked headers `spec-1296/work/1296-spec.md` and `spec-1336/work/1336-spec.md`; its archive twin already holds `config.yml`, `decisions.md`, `events.jsonl`, `manifest.yml`, `run-state.json`, `staged/`, and `spec-1296/`/`spec-1336/` subtrees. `reconcile --json` reports the directory `move-failed` on every pass, and `.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json`'s `residueFailures` entry for it reads `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rename '…/spec-1296-1336/spec-12…'` with a count of 58 — the per-spec loop's move of `spec-{n}/work` onto a twin that already has a `work/`. The tracked headers can only leave the live path through a `git mv` plus commit, which under `worktree-always: true` is a gated write from the main checkout and lands only via a worktree PR; nothing in the sweep recognizes "archive twin complete, live path holds only tracked `work/` headers" as a distinct state.

The residue bookkeeping compounds it. `residueFailures` still carries sixteen `move-failed` entries, all `escalated: true`, for paths that no longer exist live — `2026-08-31T182808-record-1679`, `2026-08-26T054601-record-1214`, `2026-08-26T055917-record-1219` (archived, zero tracked files) among them — because `recordResidueSuccess` fires only when this sweep itself archives the directory, never when a PR or a human moves it. Escalation dedups against open records only, so once a per-path record closes (the four open instances today are #1889, #1741, #1716, #1715; #1713/#1714 already closed the same way) a later pass with a stale cache entry files a fresh one for the same path.

## Deliverables

- Make the tracked-header move idempotent against an existing archive twin: when `spec-{n}/work` (or a top-level `work/`) already exists under the archive directory, compare each tracked file's blob with the twin's copy — identical → `git rm --cached`-free path: `git mv` is unnecessary, remove the live copy through git so history stays intact (`git mv` onto the twin path when the twin copy is untracked, `git rm` when the twin already tracks it); different → return a new reason `work-twin-conflict` naming both paths, never a generic `move-failed`.
- Detect the split state before any move: archive twin exists AND `git ls-files <runDir>` lists only `work/` headers AND no gitignored entries remain → classify as `archived-pending-tracked-move` (a skip reason with its own row in `docs/reconcile-checks.md`), and under `worktree-always: true` emit the paste-ready worktree/PR command that completes the move instead of counting toward `move-failed` escalation.
- Prune `residueFailures`: on every pass, drop any `move-failed`/`structurally-stuck` entry whose live path no longer exists, and when the entry was escalated, post one resolution comment on the open record (found by the existing fingerprint marker) and close it — the path resolved by other means.
- Dedup escalation against all states: `escalateResidue` searches the marker across open **and closed** records and, on a closed match whose path is still live, comments on the closed record and reopens it rather than filing a new one.
- Close #1741 (this split-state instance) when its directory archives, and close #1889/#1716/#1715 as resolved-by-other-means once the prune lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture run directory whose archive twin already contains `spec-1/work/1-spec.md` with identical content and whose live path holds only that tracked header archives cleanly on one pass; a differing twin copy returns `work-twin-conflict` and moves nothing — both pinned in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`.
- The split-state fixture under `worktree-always: true` reports `archived-pending-tracked-move` with the completing command in `skipped[]`, and its `residueFailures` count does not increment.
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/cache.test.js` pins that a `residueFailures` entry whose path is absent on disk is pruned and, when escalated, triggers exactly one close call on the marker-matched record.
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.test.js` pins that a closed marker-matched record is reopened and commented, not duplicated.
- On this checkout, `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hooks.js" reconcile --json` reports no `move-failed` entry for `2026-08-29T153740-spec-1296-1336` after the tracked headers land in `archive/` via a PR, and `reconcile-cache.json` holds no `move-failed` entry for a non-existent path.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Keep the moves-first, close-last invariant and the `revertPlainMoves` rollback. Add the twin comparison in the `workMoves` assembly (before the per-spec loop) using `git hash-object` on both copies; the split-state predicate reads `fs.readdirSync(runDir)` minus tracked paths and the twin's existence, and sits beside `isOrphanedMint`. For pruning, iterate `residueFailures` keys in `cache.js` after `archiveMerged` returns, `fs.existsSync` each path, and delegate the record close to `escalate-residue.js`'s runner seam so tests inject it. For dedup, extend the marker lookup to `--state all` (the same `findByMarker` idiom `_shared/headless-self-report.md` uses) and add the reopen branch. Document the two new reasons and the prune step in `docs/reconcile-checks.md`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveRunDir`'s `workMoves` twin comparison, per-spec loop, new `archived-pending-tracked-move` and `work-twin-conflict` reasons
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` — `residueFailures` prune after each pass
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.js` — all-state marker dedup, reopen branch, resolution comment + close
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — twin-identical, twin-conflict, split-state cases
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/cache.test.js` — prune + close-once case
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.test.js` — reopen-not-duplicate case
- `docs/reconcile-checks.md` — reason vocabulary and prune step

## Gotchas

- `revertPlainMoves` must be able to undo a partial twin merge; a `git rm` of a live tracked copy is not a plain move — do it last, after every gitignored entry has moved, so a failure before it leaves history untouched.
- Reconcile runs in-process, so its `git mv`/`git rm` are not gated by the PreToolUse hook — but the resulting commit still needs to land on `main` via the sweep's own commit path, and under `pr-first` the main checkout may lag origin (the record's step 5); read `mirror.state` before deciding the split state is stale.
- The `structurally-stuck` prune interacts with #1811 (consolidated escalation for that reason); keep the prune reason-agnostic so both classes benefit without duplicating logic.
- Reopening a closed record is an outward write reconcile already performs (filing), but it is more visible; comment first, reopen second, so a failed reopen leaves an explanatory comment.

## Original request

bin/lib/reconcile archive-merged.js: split-state run dir makes archival fail with ENOTEMPTY forever and re-files the residue record

**Summary:** `archive-merged.js`'s `fs.renameSync(dir, archiveDir)` is not idempotent for a run directory whose gitignored half was already archived while its git-tracked `spec-*/work/*-spec.md` headers stayed under the live path — every later reconcile pass fails with `ENOTEMPTY`, and the auto-filed residue record is re-filed after the first one closes.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/reconcile` — `archive-merged.js` (the `archive` check), plus the `move-failed` auto-file path in `bin/lib/reconcile`

**Repro steps:**
1. Finish a multi-spec `/flow` run whose per-spec `spec-{n}/work/{n}-spec.md` headers are committed (the normal `flow/materialize.md` audit-trail rule).
2. Let an archival pass move the run dir's gitignored half (`config.yml`, `decisions.md`, `events.jsonl`, `manifest.yml`, `staged/`, `spec-*/` scratch) into `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/{run-id}/`, but leave the tracked headers in place under the live path — this is what happens under `worktree-always: true`, where a `git mv` from the main checkout is a gated write and the tracked half can only move through a worktree PR.
3. Run `node bin/hooks.js reconcile --json` repeatedly.
4. Observe `runs[]` reporting `reason: move-failed` with `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rename '.../pipelines/{run-id}' -> '.../pipelines/archive/{run-id}'` on every pass; after 3 passes reconcile auto-files a `move-failed` record.
5. Close that record via a PR that `git mv`s the four headers into the archive path. If the main checkout has not yet fast-forwarded to that merge (its local integration branch still tracks the headers under the live path), the next passes hit the same `ENOTEMPTY` and reconcile files a second record for the same path (observed as two consecutive records in a private project).

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the archive check merges into an existing archive directory — move the remaining entries individually, or detect the split state (archive dir exists AND the live dir holds only git-tracked `work/` headers) and either complete the tracked half through a worktree/PR or classify the dir as "archived pending checkout catch-up" instead of `move-failed`. A live dir left with only tracked headers should not re-trigger the auto-file after its record has already been closed by a merged PR.
Actual: permanent `move-failed` + `ENOTEMPTY` on every pass, and a duplicate auto-filed record once the first one closes.

**Related (not duplicates):** the open per-path `reconcile: move-failed stuck on …` records (#1889, #1741, #1716, #1715) are instances this defect can keep producing; #1613 covered the skip vocabulary for non-move-failed dirs, not this rename path.

**Definition:** Clear — the ask is a single behavior (merge-into-existing-archive / split-state detection), not an open design choice.

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` Step 3.8 dispatches each project-local craft critic with, per (e), the critic's `SKILL.md` inlined verbatim (item 1, "a path string reaches nothing") and the decisions layer — `DESIGN.md` then `.impeccable/design.json` — inlined verbatim (item 3). On a project with a ~25 KB `DESIGN.md` and a ~20 KB sidecar, plus `emil-design-eng`'s ~28 KB `SKILL.md`, that is ~73 KB of prompt per critic, read into the dispatching context and written back out before the critic sees a changed line. Step 3.8 (b) selects the critic whenever `design-critique` resolves `auto`, the track is `web`, and decisions are present — it never asks whether the diff has any design surface: a 20-line change to fetch/refresh control flow in one React component (no JSX, CSS, template, or copy lines touched) dispatches the full critic exactly like a component rewrite would.

Observed on 2026-09-04 (plugin 6.114.1): the critic was fanned out alongside the Impeccable critique/audit runner and the code-simplifier; the dispatching session hit an API session limit mid-flight, all three subagent output files were 0 bytes, the critic's findings survived only via a coordinating session's relay, and re-dispatching the other two moved Impeccable's critique score from 30/40 to 25/40 on identical input. `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s Failed-agent retrieval section documents the session-limit signature but not that a parent-terminated subagent leaves a 0-byte output file, so "read its transcript tail" is not a recovery path in that case.

## Deliverables

- Add a design-surface gate to Step 3.8 (b): before selecting a critic, classify the changed UI files' hunks; when no changed line is JSX/TSX markup, CSS/style, template, or user-facing copy — control-flow-only edits — skip the critic with a `SCANNED` line naming the gate, the same posture Layer 3 already takes for non-frontend files. Implement the classification as a small deterministic helper beside `bin/lib/design-detect/` (line-level, extension- and syntax-keyed) rather than prose judgment, so the gate is testable.
- Replace the verbatim inlining of the decisions layer in Step 3.8 (e) item 3 with an instructed read: pass the absolute paths of `DESIGN.md` and the sidecar with an explicit "Read these files first, before judging" sentence, and keep only the critic's `SKILL.md` inline (item 1). Re-word the "a path string reaches nothing" rationale to what it actually guards — an unnamed, uninstructed path — so the instruction stays honest about the contract.
- Add the 0-byte-output observation to `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s Failed-agent retrieval section: a subagent whose parent session is terminated leaves an empty output file; the only record is a relay from a coordinating session, and the dispatcher must treat an empty file as "no result," never as "no findings."
- Update `critics.md`'s dispatch notes and `docs/skill-graph.md` only if the gate changes the caller edge (it should not); keep `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s sub-file table in sync if a helper file is added.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture diff touching only control-flow lines in a `.tsx` file produces no craft-critic dispatch and one `SCANNED … design-surface gate: no JSX/CSS/template/copy lines changed` line in `decisions.md`; the same file with one JSX attribute change dispatches the critic — both pinned by a unit test on the helper and a conformance test on `review.md`'s Step 3.8 text.
- A dispatched critic prompt contains the critic's `SKILL.md` inline, the two absolute paths with the "Read these files first" instruction, and no verbatim `DESIGN.md`/sidecar content; a conformance test asserts the prompt template's byte size for the reference fixture drops below 35 KB.
- `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` names the empty-output-file case and its handling; `tests/` conformance for that file passes.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

The gate is a line classifier over `git diff -U0` hunks for the files Step 2 resolved: extension first (`.css`/`.scss`/`.module.*` → style; `.html`/`.vue`/`.svelte` → template), then per-line syntax for `.jsx`/`.tsx` (a line inside a JSX return/element, a `className`/`style` attribute, or a string literal rendered as text counts as surface; imports, hooks, fetch calls, and conditionals do not). Put it in `plugin/bin/lib/design-detect/surface-lines.js` with a tiny CLI entry in `plugin/bin/design-detect.js` (`--surface-lines <diff>`), so Step 3.8 (b) calls one command and branches on its JSON. For the prompt change, edit (e) items 1 and 3 and the rationale sentence together, and leave the direction-contract block (Step 3.7's `impeccable-finish-reviewer` input) untouched — it is a different dispatch with its own contract. The contract note is one paragraph under Failed-agent retrieval.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` — Step 3.8 (b) gate, (e) items 1/3 and the "path reaches nothing" rationale
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/critics.md` — dispatch note for the instructed-read shape
- `plugin/skills/_shared/design-craft.md` — the "Subagent Contract compliance" paragraph item 1's rationale cites; reword it alongside item 1
- `plugin/bin/lib/design-detect/surface-lines.js` — new line classifier (new file)
- `plugin/bin/design-detect.js` — `--surface-lines` entry
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — Failed-agent retrieval: empty-output-file case
- `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/` — classifier unit tests (new file beside the existing suite)
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — sub-file/CLI table entry for the new helper

## Gotchas

- Do not gate on file extension alone: the incident's file was `.tsx`, which Layer 3 correctly classifies as frontend — the gate has to look at changed lines, not file type.
- The instructed-read shape depends on the critic agent having the `Read` tool; `critics.md`'s roster entries are project-local `.claude/agents/*.md` files whose tool lists may restrict it — check each roster row and fall back to inlining for a critic without `Read`.
- Impeccable's own critique score is non-deterministic across runs (30 → 25 on identical input); do not let the conformance test assert on critique output.
- Step 3.7's finish-reviewer dispatch is a third-party exempt agent with its own input contract; this record changes only Step 3.8.

## Original request

design-wrapper review: craft-critic dispatch inlines ~70 KB per critic; a 3-agent fan-out on a 20-line control-flow diff tripped an API session limit

**Summary:** design-wrapper review Step 3.8 inlines ~70 KB per craft critic (SKILL.md + DESIGN.md + sidecar verbatim); a three-agent review fan-out on a 20-line control-flow diff tripped an API session limit and lost every in-flight result.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** design-wrapper (modes/review.md, Step 3.8 craft-critic dispatch)

**Use case:** Reviewing a 20-line diff in one React client component where only fetch/refresh control flow changed (no JSX, CSS, or copy lines) in a project that has a DESIGN.md (~25 KB) and an `.impeccable/design.json` sidecar (~20 KB). Under `design-critique: auto` with decisions present, Step 3.8 (b) selects `emil-design-eng`, and (e) requires the critic's SKILL.md (~28 KB), DESIGN.md, and the sidecar to be inlined verbatim into the Task prompt ("a path string reaches nothing"). That is ~73 KB of prompt read into the dispatching context and written back out before the critic sees a single changed line, for a diff with no design surface to judge.

What happened: the dispatching session fanned out the critic alongside the Impeccable critique/audit runner and the code-simplifier and was terminated by an API session limit mid-flight. All three subagent output files were 0 bytes; the critic's findings survived only because a coordinating session had relayed a summary, and the other two agents had to be re-dispatched (Impeccable's critique score moved 30/40 -> 25/40 between the two runs on identical input).

Either of these would close the gap:

1. Let the dispatch reference the three files by absolute path with an explicit "Read these first" instruction, keeping only the (small) SKILL.md inline. The "path reaches nothing" concern is about an unnamed path, not an instructed read.
2. Add a scope gate to Step 3.8 (b): skip the critic when the changed UI files contain no JSX/CSS/template/copy line changes -- a control-flow-only diff has no design surface for a craft critic to judge -- the same way Layer 3 already skips non-frontend files.

Related observation for `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`: a subagent whose parent is terminated leaves a 0-byte output file, so "read its transcript" is not a recovery path in that case -- a relay from a coordinating session is the only record.

**Definition:** Clear

Surface: infra

## Current State

`materialize.js` computes `drift` only from a record's `Verified-as-of: {sha}` body-metadata line (`extractVerifiedAsOf` in `bin/lib/issues/record.js`; `computeDrift` in `plugin/bin/materialize.js`), and a stale stamp produces one stderr sentence ("premise is N commits old … re-derive facts against current HEAD before implementing") and an envelope field; it never stops or re-measures. `drift` is `null` for any record without the stamp — which is every record not filed by the four health sweeps, the only callers that thread `specShapedBody`'s `verifiedAsOf` param (`bin/harness-health.js`, `docs-health.js`, `code-health.js`, `journey-health.js` via their `issue-payload.js`). `flow/materialize.md`'s "Freshness-stamp drift (#117)" and "Named-location drift (#315)" paragraphs describe exactly this.

Wrap-up's CLAUDE.md & rules row opens on the `claudeMdOverBudget` fact (`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/facts.js`, `computeClaudeMdOverBudget`), which returns a bare boolean — it discards which target was over and by how much — and the row's filing (`skills/wrap-up/claude-md-curation.md` via `_shared/harness-health-analysis.md`, surfaced as a Console queue write) composes its backlog record without `verifiedAsOf`. So an over-budget record carries a measured claim ("205 lines vs the 150 budget") that no later phase can date or re-measure.

Observed on plugin 6.114.1 in a private project: the record was filed at 205 lines; two days later another record brought the file to 146; a dispatch then built the over-budget record through a full build/review cycle, with `drift: null` at materialize, `claudeMdOverBudget` already `false` at the base, and the premise discovered only at plan time. `_shared/reverify-before-write.md` states the measure-before-you-act posture for writes; nothing applies it to a record's stated premise at run start. #1769 (shaped by this sweep) adds an `ASSUMPTION — verify at build` marker for claims the composer cannot settle; this record is the complementary mechanical case, where the claim *is* a command.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Measured fact, not a boolean.** `facts.js`: keep `claudeMdOverBudget` (boolean, read by `engine-plan.js` and `registry.js`'s gate) and add a sibling fact `claudeMdBudgetTargets: [{path, lines, budget}]` for every in-scope target, computed in the same pass. Expand-contract: no existing consumer changes; the curation row reads the new fact.
- [ ] **Stamp the filing.** `claude-md-curation.md`: the over-budget record composed by the row's queue write goes through `specShapedBody` with `verifiedAsOf` set to the sha wrap-up read the repo at (the same HEAD `wrap-up-pack.json`'s `state` probe records), a Current State line per over-budget target in the form `` `{path}`: {lines} lines vs the {budget}-line budget (`wc -l {path}` at {sha}) ``, and a new optional body-metadata line `Premise-check: {command}` whose command exits 0 while the premise still holds — for this filing, one `test $(wc -l < {path}) -gt {budget}` per target, joined with `&&` when several.
- [ ] **Materialize runs the premise check.** `record.js`: `extractPremiseCheck(body)` for the `Premise-check:` line, documented beside `VERIFIED_AS_OF_RE` as an optional single-line metadata field. `materialize.js`: when present, run it from the checkout root with the CLI's usual short timeout and add `premise: { command, exit, satisfiedAtBase }` to the envelope (`satisfiedAtBase: true` when exit is non-zero); `null` when the line is absent. On `satisfiedAtBase`, print one stderr sentence in the drift sentence's shape ("premise already satisfied at base: `{command}` exited {n}") and, under a run dir, log a `STAGED` decision (`_shared/auto-decision-log.md`) with a staged note in `staged/` proposing to close the record as already satisfied — never a silent proceed, never a hard stop from the CLI.
- [ ] **Build acts on it.** `flow/materialize.md` gains a "Premise check" paragraph beside the two drift paragraphs; `build/SKILL.md`'s Spec Step 2 (existing-progress check) reads `premise.satisfiedAtBase` from the envelope and, when true, routes to the Review Console's staged close rather than planning — the same surface an unattended run already uses for staged proposals.
- [ ] **Tests.** `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/facts.test.js` (or the sibling that pins `computeClaudeMdOverBudget`): targets list populated with `lines`/`budget`, boolean unchanged. `tests/materialize-drift.test.js` sibling `tests/materialize-premise-check.test.js`: no line → `premise: null`; exit 0 → `satisfiedAtBase: false`; exit 1 → `true` plus the stderr sentence; a throwing runner degrades to `null`, never a crash (mirroring the drift tests' shapes). A prose pin asserting `claude-md-curation.md` names `verifiedAsOf` and `Premise-check:`, and `materialize.md` carries the paragraph.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A wrap-up run whose CLAUDE.md exceeds its budget files a record whose body carries `Verified-as-of: {sha}`, the measured `{lines} vs {budget}` line per target, and a `Premise-check:` line; `materialize.js` on that record reports non-null `drift` and non-null `premise`.
2. `computeClaudeMdOverBudget` still returns the same boolean for every fixture in the existing facts test; `claudeMdBudgetTargets` lists each in-scope target with `lines` and `budget`.
3. `node bin/materialize.js #N` on a record whose `Premise-check:` command exits non-zero prints the "premise already satisfied at base" sentence, sets `premise.satisfiedAtBase: true`, and (with `--run-dir`) writes a `STAGED` line and a staged close note; a record with no `Premise-check:` line behaves byte-identically to today.
4. `build/SKILL.md` Spec Step 2 names `premise.satisfiedAtBase` and routes it to the Console's staged close; `flow/materialize.md` documents `Premise-check:` beside the drift paragraphs.
5. `npm test` green; every existing case in `tests/materialize-drift.test.js` and the facts tests unchanged.
6. Replaying the reported sequence in a fixture (file over budget at filing, under budget at base) ends with a staged close proposal and no plan authored; quoted in the PR description.

## Technical Approach

Two hops, both additive: the filing side gets what the health sweeps already have (a stamp) plus the one thing a mechanical premise needs (its command); the materialize side gains one optional metadata line and one optional envelope field. Do not generalize to "re-measure any Current State that looks mechanical" — the filing site knows its command, the reader should not guess one (#1769 covers the non-mechanical case with a marker). The `Premise-check:` command runs in the checkout being materialized, so it is inherently repo-local; the record composer must write only commands that need no network and no plugin path.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/facts.js` — `claudeMdBudgetTargets` sibling fact beside `computeClaudeMdOverBudget`
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/claude-md-curation.md` — over-budget filing: `verifiedAsOf`, measured line, `Premise-check:` line
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/record.js` — `extractPremiseCheck` beside `extractVerifiedAsOf`; `specShapedBody` renders the optional line
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` — run the check; `premise` envelope field; stderr sentence; staged close under `--run-dir`
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — "Premise check" paragraph
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — Spec Step 2 routing on `premise.satisfiedAtBase`
- `tests/materialize-premise-check.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/facts.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- `specShapedBody` enforces sha shape on `verifiedAsOf`; pass a full or 7+ hex sha, never a ref name.
- Body-metadata lines are plain lines before the first `##`, never YAML frontmatter (`materialize.md`'s own convention note); `Premise-check:` follows the same rule and must be single-line.
- The check runs an arbitrary shell command from a record body — bound it to the filing site's own composer (this plugin writes it), document that materialize runs it, and keep the timeout short; a hostile or broken command degrades to `premise: null` with a stderr note, never a crash (same posture as `computeDrift`'s throwing-runner test).
- `engine-plan.js`'s `claudeMdOverBudget` open/closed labels are pinned by tests; the boolean's name and semantics must not change.

## Original request

**Summary:** A work record filed by wrap-up's CLAUDE.md & rules row from the `claudeMdOverBudget` signal ("CLAUDE.md is 205 lines vs the 150 budget") was later dispatched after an unrelated compression had already brought the file to 146 lines; because the filing carries no `Verified-as-of` stamp, `flow/materialize.md`'s freshness-stamp and named-location drift checks read `null`, and the build phase only discovered at plan time that the acceptance criterion was already met at the branch base.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` — `skills/wrap-up/claude-md-curation.md`'s over-budget filing; `skills/flow/materialize.md` — "Freshness-stamp drift (#117)" / "Named-location drift (#315)"

**Use case:** In a private project, wrap-up's CLAUDE.md & rules row filed a record for an over-budget CLAUDE.md (measured at 205 lines). Two days later a separate record compressed the Don'ts to 146 lines. A dispatch firing then claimed and built the over-budget record: materialize's drift stamp was `null` (the filing is not produced by a health sweep, so `specShapedBody`'s `verifiedAsOf` was never set), the plugin fact check `claudeMdOverBudget` already read `false` at build time, and the pipeline still ran a full build/review cycle whose only remaining value was restructuring (a `paths:`-scoped rule) rather than the trim the record asked for. The build disclosed the drift in the PR body and a follow-up record, but nothing stopped or re-scoped the run at the point where the premise was measurable. Two possible fixes, either would do: (1) have the `claudeMdOverBudget` filing stamp `Verified-as-of: {sha}` (and the measured number) the same way the four health sweeps do, so materialize's existing drift check has something to compare; and/or (2) let materialize re-measure a record whose Current State names a mechanical check (`wc -l CLAUDE.md`, a line budget) and surface "premise already satisfied at base" as a first-class stop/decision before the build starts — the same "measure before you act" posture `_shared/reverify-before-write.md` already takes for writes.

**Definition:** Clear — the filing site and the drift check both exist; the gap is the missing stamp between them.

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1
