Surface: infra

## Current State
`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` keeps four session-scoped exclusion files, each with its own shape, producer, reader, and report:

| File | Shape | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dispatch-blocked-excluded.json` | `{number, blockedBy: number[]}[]` | `queue-pull-script.md` (removed from the pool) | `blocked-exclusion-report.md` |
| `dispatch-open-pr-excluded.json` | `{number, pr}[]` | `queue-pull-script.md` (removed from the pool) | `open-pr-exclusion-report.md`; SKILL.md's `#N` / `#N,#M` forms (reason lookup, #1973) |
| `dispatch-oversized-excluded.json` | `{records: number[], size, threshold}[]` | `queue-pull-script.md` (stays in the pool) | `next-ranking.md` (excludes), `oversized-group-report.md` |
| `dispatch-firing-excluded.json` | `number[]` | SKILL.md's Loop per `firing-exclusion.md` (append per iteration) | `next-ranking.md` (excludes) |

Every one is read with an inline `fs.existsSync(p) ? require(p) : []` and filtered with hand-written `Set` logic inside a `node -e` block embedded in the skill's markdown; `next-ranking.md`'s bash block alone carries two different key derivations (`keyOf(g)` for oversized record-sets, member membership for firing numbers). The next exclusion reason (a residue class, a maintainer deny-list, a freshness veto) copies the pattern a fifth time or forces this refactor later. No `bin/` module owns the concept: `bin/lib/dispatch/` holds `artifact-verdict.js`, `ceremony-derive.js`, `queue-order.js` only.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `bin/lib/dispatch/exclusions.js`: one module owning the shape and the file — `readExclusions(path)` → `{ reason, records: number[], detail }[]` (absent/unreadable → `[]`), `appendExclusion(path, entry)`, `excludedNumbers(entries, reasons)` → `Set<number>`, and `groupIsExcluded(group, entries, reasons)` (true when any member is in the set, the semantics `firing-exclusion.md` and `next-ranking.md` already use), with unit tests in `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js`.
- [ ] One session-scoped `dispatch-exclusions.json` replacing the four files: `queue-pull-script.md` writes `blocked` (`detail: { blockedBy }`), `open-pr` (`detail: { pr }`), and `oversized` (`detail: { size, threshold }`) entries through `appendExclusion` after truncating the file at the start of its run; SKILL.md's Loop appends `firing` entries through the same call per `firing-exclusion.md`'s rule (unchanged trigger conditions).
- [ ] `next-ranking.md`'s script filters with `groupIsExcluded(g, entries, ['oversized', 'firing'])` — one derivation, no `keyOf` vs member split; the `#N` / `#N,#M` reason lookup reads `open-pr` entries from the same file.
- [ ] The three report files and `blocked-exclusion-report.md` read the one file filtered by reason, rendering byte-identical lines to today; `firing-exclusion.md` and `dispatch/SKILL.md` name the new file and the reason vocabulary.
- [ ] `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js` (which extracts and executes `next-ranking.md`'s bash block) updated to seed `dispatch-exclusions.json` entries instead of two files; `tests/session-tmp-root-migration.test.js` and `tests/node-e-snippet-syntax.test.js` stay green (they scan the same blocks).
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md` gains the new module wherever it lists `bin/lib/{name}/` modules (it names the directory convention, not each file, today — add a line only if a per-module list exists); `_shared/session-tmp-root.md` enumerates no dispatch file names, so it needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Exactly one session-scoped exclusion file is written or read anywhere under `plugin/skills/dispatch/`; `grep -rn "excluded.json" plugin/skills` returns no match.
2. All four reasons survive with their current pool semantics: `blocked` and `open-pr` still remove candidates from `dispatch-groups.json` in the queue pull; `oversized` and `firing` still leave groups in the pool and are excluded only by the ranking script.
3. Each report renders the same line text as before for the same inputs; the `#N` form still names the linked PR for an `open-pr` exclusion.
4. `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js`'s four scenarios (absent file, one excluded group, all excluded → `null`, bundle-member match) pass against the new shape; `exclusions.js` has its own unit coverage; `npm test` is green.
5. Adding a fifth reason requires one `appendExclusion` call site and one report, no new file or filter logic — demonstrated by a test that seeds an unknown reason and shows the ranking ignores it while `readExclusions` returns it.

## Technical Approach
Move the concept into code and leave the skills as callers: the markdown scripts already shell out to `node -e` with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/lib/...` requires, so `require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/lib/dispatch/exclusions.js')` inside those blocks is the same pattern `session-tmp.js` is loaded with today. One file rather than one-per-reason: the readers already differ only by reason, and a single array with a `reason` field is what makes the fifth reason a one-line append. Keep the pool split (`blocked`/`open-pr` removed at queue pull; `oversized`/`firing` filtered at ranking) exactly as is — the record is about the file mechanism, not the exclusion semantics.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — the `files` map and the three producer writes.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/next-ranking.md` — the `files` map, the `firingExcluded`/`oversizedKeys` filter.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/firing-exclusion.md` — the append rule.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md` — Loop paragraph; `#N` / `#N,#M` bullets (#1973 reason lookup).
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/blocked-exclusion-report.md`, `open-pr-exclusion-report.md`, `oversized-group-report.md` — readers.
- `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/` — new `exclusions.js` beside `queue-order.js`.
- `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/` — script-executing test and new unit test.

## Gotchas
- `dispatch-blocked-excluded-body.json` is an intermediate of the body-text blocker pass, not an exclusion list; leave it alone.
- The reports' "drain + zero-eligible silence" exception keys on report content, not file presence; reading one file for all reasons must not change when a report is omitted.
- `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js` extracts the bash block by a fenced-code regex; keep the block's fence and the `eval "$(node -e …)"` prologue shape so the extraction still matches.
- Truncate-then-append in the queue pull must happen once at the start of `queue-pull-script.md`, before the blocked pass — the firing entries appended by the Loop live in the same file and must survive the per-iteration re-pull, so the truncation drops only non-`firing` entries (`readExclusions` → filter → rewrite), never the whole file.

## Original request

Whole-branch pre-release review finding (v6.113.0 -> origin/main, d68ffa7d9..7036ce768): the next exclusion reason will either copy this one-off pattern a fifth time or require a larger later refactor to unify what should have been one mechanism from the start.

Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` walks `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/` twice per session start. The stale-runs report pulls up to `MAX_REPORTED` entries from `context.js`'s `iterRunDirsWithState(ctx.cwd)`, which anchors to the main checkout, sorts newest-first, reads each `run-state.json`, skips `status: 'clean'` runs, and skips runs whose `archive/{name}` twin is `clean` or freshly `archiving`. The #1493 AC5 staged-proposals scan, a few lines below, needs the opposite status filter (only `clean` runs, name-matched to `-(tidy|sweep)-standalone`, with a non-empty `staged/`) and therefore re-implements the walk by hand: its own `mainCheckoutRoot` anchor, its own `readdirSync` + name filter + sort + reverse, its own `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(run-state.json))` per dir, and its own early-break at `MAX_REPORTED`. Its comment says why: the iterator "deliberately excludes status `clean` runs … so it needs its own directory read". The hand-rolled copy also lacks the iterator's archive-twin and `archiving`-claim skips, so a clean standalone run whose archival is mid-flight can still be listed. Both blocks then build the same advisory shape by hand: `- {name} — {detail}` lines, a header sentence, and the #803 relay trailer.

`bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `iterCleanRunDirs` (#1733) is a third copy of the same clean-only walk, without the anchor and without the twin skips.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `iterRunDirsWithState(cwd, { status } = {})` in `context.js`: an optional `status` filter — `'clean'` yields only clean runs, absent keeps today's exclude-clean behavior byte-for-byte — applied at the one existing status check so the anchor, ordering, archive-twin skip, and `archiving`-claim skip are shared by both shapes. `listRunDirsWithState`/`listRunDirs` pass the option through unchanged in their default form.
- [ ] `session-start.js`'s staged-proposals scan becomes a `for … of iterRunDirsWithState(ctx.cwd, { status: 'clean' })` loop that keeps only its own two concerns: the `-(tidy|sweep)-standalone` name test on `path.basename(dir)` and the non-empty `staged/` read, with the existing `MAX_REPORTED` early break. The hand-rolled `readdirSync`/sort/`run-state.json` read is deleted.
- [ ] One `advisoryBanner(header, lines, trailer)` helper in `session-start.js` used by both the stale-runs and staged-proposals blocks, producing byte-identical strings to today's inline concatenation (the tests below are the proof).
- [ ] `archive-merged.js`'s `iterCleanRunDirs(root)` reduced to `[...iterRunDirsWithState(root, { status: 'clean' })]`, so the third copy disappears; its callers and the `{ dir, state }` shape are unchanged.
- [ ] Tests: `tests/hooks-context.test.js` cases for the option (default excludes clean; `{ status: 'clean' }` yields only clean; both shapes honor the archive-twin skip); the existing #1493/#1494 cases in `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` pass unmodified; one new session-start case that a clean `-tidy-standalone` run with a `clean` archive twin is not listed (the skip the hand-rolled walk lacked).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `session-start.js` contains no `fs.readdirSync` of the pipelines directory and no direct `run-state.json` parse; both advisory scans iterate `iterRunDirsWithState`.
2. With no option, `iterRunDirsWithState` yields exactly what it yields today for every existing fixture (the `hooks-context`, `session-start`, `archive-merged`, `console-execute`, and residue-probe suites are the proof).
3. The two banners' rendered text is byte-identical to today's for the existing fixtures.
4. `iterCleanRunDirs` in `archive-merged.js` no longer walks the directory itself; the #1544 clean-status sweep cases pass unmodified.
5. `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
An opt-in filter, not a widened yield: #1733 declined changing the iterator's *default* output because eight callers rely on the clean exclusion; an option that leaves the default untouched changes nothing for them and lets the two clean-only walkers stop re-deriving the anchor and skips. Implement the option at the single `if (state && state.status === 'clean') continue;` line — `const wantClean = opts.status === 'clean'; if (Boolean(state && state.status === 'clean') !== wantClean) continue;` — so the archive-twin and `archiving` checks below it apply to both shapes. Land after #1733 (which touches `iterCleanRunDirs`'s caller) so the swap here is a contained one-line body replacement.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `iterRunDirsWithState`, `listRunDirsWithState`, `listRunDirs`, `RUN_ID_RE`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` — the stale-runs block and the #1493 AC5 staged-proposals block (both under `run()`), `MAX_REPORTED`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `iterCleanRunDirs`.
- `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` — #1493 AC5 / I2 / I4 / #1494 cases; `tests/hooks-context.test.js`; `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` (#1544 cases).

## Gotchas
- The hand-rolled scan swallows an unreadable `run-state.json` with `continue`; the iterator yields `state: null` for such a dir and the `status` check must treat `null` as not-clean under both shapes, so the swap keeps skipping it.
- `MAX_REPORTED` applies after the name and `staged/` filters in the staged-proposals scan (it counts approvable entries, not candidates); keep the early break on `approvable.length`, not on iteration count.
- The long #1493 comment block explaining why the scan needed its own read must be rewritten, not deleted: the reason it cites is exactly what the option removes.
- `docs/hooks.md` mentions the stale-run report by behavior only; no docs change unless the iterator's option is worth a sentence there (judgment call at build).

## Original request
## Current State
The #1493 AC5 staged-proposals advisory scan in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` (~line 88) hand-rolls its own `fs.readdirSync` + filter + sort + per-dir-state-read loop instead of extending `context.js`'s `iterRunDirsWithState` (already used a few lines above for the stale-runs report) — because that iterator hardcodes skipping 'clean' status runs and this scan wants only clean ones. It also duplicates the advisory-banner-building pattern (MAX_REPORTED capping, "- name — detail" lines, templated trailer) of the block just above it.

## Deliverables
Add an `includeClean` option to `iterRunDirsWithState` (or equivalent) so session-start.js's clean-only scan reuses the shared iterator instead of a second, differently-filtered directory-walking implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] session-start.js's staged-proposals scan uses the shared iterator rather than a standalone readdir/sort/per-dir-read loop.
- [ ] Existing session-start hook tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Full `npm test` passes.

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger — changes iterRunDirsWithState's shared contract, not a localized single-file change; found by the pre-v6.112.0 whole-branch review.

## Current State
`isAbandonedInterrupted(runDir, state, sessionId, now)` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` calls `hasReadableEventsLog(runDir)` and then `lastOwnEventMs(runDir)` back to back. Each does its own `fs.readFileSync(path.join(runDir, 'events.jsonl'))`: the first only to learn whether the read succeeds (an unreadable or absent log is UNKNOWN evidence, per #1673 F9, never proof of staleness), the second to parse every line, drop `attribution === 'fallback'` events, and return the newest parseable `ts`. Two reads of the same file per candidate run dir, per reconcile pass. `hasReadableEventsLog` exists only because `lastOwnEventMs`'s `null` conflates "unreadable" with "readable but no qualifying event".

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js`'s `scanWrapupEvents(runDir)` is documented as "the single reader for the paired appendEvent writer", but it is not a drop-in: it returns `{ any, wrapup }` over `skill_invoked` events only, carries no timestamps, and deliberately does not filter fallback-attributed lines — the comment above `lastOwnEventMs` says the two filters are intentionally asymmetric and must not be reconciled. So the record's "ideally reuse `scanWrapupEvents`" half cannot be taken literally; what can be shared is the raw read-and-parse below both consumers.

## Deliverables
- [ ] A shared line reader in `context.js`, `readEventLines(runDir)` → `null` when `events.jsonl` is absent or unreadable, else an array of parsed event objects (unparseable lines skipped), exported alongside `scanWrapupEvents`; `scanWrapupEvents` reimplemented on top of it with identical output.

Surface: infra

## Current State
`archiveMerged()` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` ends with two loops that run the same merged-PR archive sequence: the main loop over `iterRunDirsWithState(root)` and the #1544 clean-status sweep over `iterCleanRunDirs(root)`. Both do `resolvePrState(root, branch)` → `readConsoleState(dir)` → `decideArchive(prState, consoleState)` → skip on `decision.action === 'skip'` → `localHasMerge(root, prState.mergeCommit)` with the `local-behind-merge` / `merge-commit-unknown` skip reasons → `dryRun` short-circuit → `archiveRunDir(root, dir)` → `trackArchiveResult(root, repoSlug, dir, result)` → push to `archived`/`skipped`. The copies already differ in one place that the duplication hides: the main loop's `decideArchive` skip also calls `trackStuckSkip(root, repoSlug, dir, decision.reason)` (#1613's structurally-stuck visibility), the clean loop's does not.

The two loops need different inputs only at the front: the main loop derives `branch` from the worktree list (with the structurally-stuck skip on `no-worktree`/`no-branch`), the clean loop from `fallbackBranch(root, dir, state)` because a `clean` run's `state.worktree` is null by construction. `iterCleanRunDirs` exists because `iterRunDirsWithState` in `bin/lib/hooks/context.js` skips `status: 'clean'` by design, and that generator has eight callers (hooks dispatcher, session-start, console-execute, the residue probe, the stray-run-dir sweep, reconcile's index) that all rely on the exclusion.

## Deliverables
- [ ] One helper in `archive-merged.js`, `archiveMergedRun({ root, repoSlug, dir, branch, dryRun, onSkip })` → `{ outcome: 'archived' | 'skipped', reason? }`, holding the full sequence from `resolvePrState` through `trackArchiveResult`; `onSkip(reason)` is the hook the main loop uses to call `trackStuckSkip` on a `decideArchive` skip, so the one existing difference becomes an explicit parameter rather than a divergence.
- [ ] Both loops call the helper: the main loop after its worktree-derived `branch` and structurally-stuck handling, the clean loop after `fallbackBranch`; each keeps only its branch derivation and its `archived`/`skipped` push.
- [ ] `iterRunDirsWithState`'s contract is unchanged and `iterCleanRunDirs` stays as the clean-status enumerator; the record's alternative (a state-tagged tuple from the shared iterator) is declined — see Technical Approach.
- [ ] `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`: existing cases unmodified and green; one new case that a clean-status run whose `decideArchive` skips reports the skip reason without invoking `trackStuckSkip` (pins the `onSkip` asymmetry as intended, so a later reader does not "fix" it), and one that a main-loop skip still does.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `archive-merged.js` contains exactly one call site each for `resolvePrState`, `decideArchive`, `localHasMerge`, and `archiveRunDir` inside `archiveMerged()`'s merged-PR path (the helper); neither loop body calls them directly.
2. For every existing fixture, `archiveMerged({ dryRun: true })` returns the same `archived`/`skipped` sets as before the change.
3. `iterRunDirsWithState` in `bin/lib/hooks/context.js` is byte-identical; no other caller changes.
4. The `trackStuckSkip`-on-main-loop-only behavior is preserved and pinned by a test.
5. `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Share the sequence at the caller, not the iterator. Widening `iterRunDirsWithState` to yield `clean` runs behind a tag would touch a generator that every hook invocation drives (`context.js`'s own comment: it "drives both the fallback event-attribution scan and every reconcile check's enumeration") and force each of its other callers to filter the new tuple, for a benefit that is entirely local to `archiveMerged()`. The helper is a pure extraction: move the shared block into a function whose only free variables are the ones both loops already have in scope. Land this before #1732 where possible — #1732's per-kind action switch then dispatches the `merged` kind straight to this helper instead of inlining the sequence a third time. Same file as #1732, #1734, #1737: sequence, never build in parallel.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveMerged` (both loops), `iterCleanRunDirs`, `decideArchive`, `localHasMerge`, `archiveRunDir`, `trackArchiveResult`, `trackStuckSkip`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `iterRunDirsWithState` (read for the contract; unchanged).
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js` — `fallbackBranch` (clean loop's branch source; unchanged).
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — the #1544 clean-status fixture (around the `status: 'clean', worktree: null, pr: { branch: … }` case) is the template for the new pins.

## Gotchas
- `resolvePrState` (imported from `pr-state.js`) reads the reconcile PR cache; keep it inside the helper so a future change to its caching cannot land in one loop only.
- The clean loop's comment block (#1544 rationale: why `state.worktree` is null and why `fallbackBranch` is the right source) must stay on the clean loop, not move into the helper — it explains the input, not the sequence.
- `dryRun` pushes to `archived` without touching disk in both loops today; the helper returns `outcome: 'archived'` for that case and the caller pushes, so the dry-run contract stays identical.

## Original request
## Current State
`iterCleanRunDirs()` and its consuming loop (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`, ~line 734/897) duplicate the main loop's `prState`/`decideArchive`/`localHasMerge`/`archiveRunDir`/`trackArchiveResult` sequence almost verbatim, added because `iterRunDirsWithState` excludes 'clean' status runs by design rather than generalizing the iterator/caller to yield a state-tagged tuple both loops could share.

## Deliverables
Generalize the iterator (or the caller) so both the main loop and the clean-run-dir loop share one archive-decision sequence instead of two independently maintained copies.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Only one implementation of the prState/decideArchive/localHasMerge/archiveRunDir/trackArchiveResult sequence exists.
- [ ] Existing `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` behavior is preserved.
- [ ] Full `npm test` passes.

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js`'s `mergedEvidence()` passes a caller-derived ref name as a bare positional argument to git at two call sites:

- `runGit(['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', branch, integration], root)`
- `runGit(['cherry', integration, branch], root)`

This repo's `gh-api-module-pattern` skill states the rule directly: a caller-supplied value beginning with `-` is still read as an option, and for `git` the separator is `--end-of-options`, not `--` (`--` only guards the pathspec argument slot, a different position). `docs/incident-log.md` carries the same rule for `rev-parse`/`merge-base`.

Record #1463 added a third call in the same file (`hasCommitSinceRunStart`'s `git log`) and adopted `--end-of-options` there, per CLAUDE.md's "adopt new conventions in new code first, then migrate existing ones deliberately". These two call sites are the deliberate migration that convention-adoption implies.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `mergedEvidence()`'s `merge-base --is-ancestor` call places `--end-of-options` before the two ref arguments.
- [ ] `mergedEvidence()`'s `git cherry` call does the same.
- [ ] No behavior change for any ref name git can actually produce — the existing `tests/run-integrity.test.js` AC1/AC2/AC3a cases stay green unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both call sites in `mergedEvidence()` pass their ref arguments after an `--end-of-options` separator.
2. `node --test tests/run-integrity.test.js` passes with no test edits required.
3. `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach
Two argument-array edits, no logic change: insert `'--end-of-options'` immediately before the first ref argument in each call — `['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', '--end-of-options', branch, integration]` and `['cherry', '--end-of-options', integration, branch]`. `hasCommitSinceRunStart`'s `git log` call in the same file is the in-file model (it already places `--end-of-options` before `branch`, followed by `--` for the pathspec slot); `git cherry` takes no pathspec, so no trailing `--` there.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js` — `mergedEvidence()` (the `merge-base --is-ancestor` and `cherry` calls), `hasCommitSinceRunStart()` (existing `--end-of-options` example).
- `tests/run-integrity.test.js` — AC1 (ancestor), AC2 (cherry), AC3a (unmerged) cases pin the behavior; no edits expected.

## Gotchas
- Not exploitable today: `branch` reaches these calls only from `deriveBranch()`'s parse of `git worktree list --porcelain`, and git refuses to create a ref beginning with `-`.
- `--end-of-options` requires git 2.24+; the file's existing `rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options` and `git log … --end-of-options` calls already assume it, so this adds no new floor.
- The guard just above the calls compares `branch` to `bareIntegrationName(integration)` (#1861/#1862) but passes `integration` through unnormalized; the separator protects the argument slot and changes nothing about that comparison.

## Original request

Origin: `/claude-tweaks:review #1463`, Step 3 — both dispatched lenses (3b Security, 3c Error Handling) independently reported the same location; 3c cited this repo's own `gh-api-module-pattern` skill for the rule. Staged rather than fixed inside #1463 because those two call sites are untouched by that record's diff and fixing them there would have widened it beyond its declared scope, against this project's surgical-changes rule. Filed via the `/claude-tweaks:flow #1463,#1672,#1673,#1674` consolidated Review Console.

## Current State

During record #1276's wrap-up Phase 2 (ROUTE), the Skills-row curation judge followed `.claude/skills/skill-prose-conformance-tests/SKILL.md`'s own "Record the audit" step, which invokes `harness-health.js validate-findings`. That step pushed a commit (`dad090519`) to the remote `health-state` tracking branch — a git mutation. The judge's dispatch prompt, composed per `plugin/skills/wrap-up/curation-engine.md` section 4, explicitly forbids any git mutation ("never run git add, git commit, or any other git mutation"), on the grounds that the controller alone commits, serially, after auditing each finding. The judge grepped the dispatcher for `git`/`spawnSync` beforehand and found nothing — the durable-state write lives on a path that grep missed (inside `harness-health.js`'s own audit-recording mechanism, invoked as a documented step of the project skill it was applying, not as a git command the judge composed itself).

Blast radius was contained: the push landed only on `health-state` (2 files, cursor/run bookkeeping — never the feature branch, never `main`), recorded zero findings, and left the worktree HEAD and working tree exactly as the judge's own edits left them. But the underlying gap is real: `curation-engine.md`'s dispatch contract has no carve-out for a project skill's own legitimate, sanctioned bookkeeping writes to a dedicated tracking branch, so a judge following a project skill's documented procedure can violate the contract without realizing it — the contract and the project skill disagree, and nothing in either file resolves the disagreement.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide the resolution direction: either (a) `curation-engine.md`'s dispatch-prompt git-mutation prohibition gets an explicit carve-out for a project skill's own sanctioned bookkeeping branch writes (name the pattern — a push to a branch distinct from the worktree's own feature branch and from the integration branch, or an explicit allowlist), or (b) `.claude/skills/skill-prose-conformance-tests/SKILL.md`'s "Record the audit" step gains a precondition that skips the write when invoked from a context whose contract forbids git mutation (e.g. a documented env var or a passed flag the dispatch prompt sets).
- [ ] Implement the chosen direction.
- [ ] Add a conformance test or explicit inline note documenting the resolved contract, so a future dispatch-contract change doesn't silently reintroduce the conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A Skills-row (or any other curation-engine.md fan-out/singleton) judge dispatch, run against a project whose applicable skill file includes a git-mutating audit-recording step, either completes the write safely under a stated, narrow exception, or the write is skipped with the skip logged — never an unnoticed, unauthorized push.
2. `npm test` passes.

The removal date (2026-11-16) has **not** yet passed as of this record's shaping (2026-08-17) — it is roughly three months out. This record documents and prepares the contract phase; it does not authorize building the removal before that date.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Remove the flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys from `permittedGrants`'s return value in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, and delete the module-header comment block documenting the now-resolved removal condition.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (the `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` pattern and its explanatory comment), reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly.

Decide whether this stays as-is (the per-grant shape already fixes the *granted*-path pairing bug; the withheld-grant sharing is a separate, lower-severity residue) or gets its own follow-up record.
  2. The granted path's flat `reason` today carries positive rationale text ("class is clean, ceiling is unattended, grant origination opted in") that no per-grant key reproduces. Decide whether to populate that positive rationale into the granted per-grant `reason` field, or record explicitly (in a code comment) that it is intentionally dropped as noise once the grant itself is visible via `granted: true`.
- [ ] Update or remove the flat-key compat tests in the `bin-lib/issues` test suite to match the per-grant-only shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hard precondition, checked first:** the build only proceeds once the current date is on or after 2026-11-16. A build attempted before that date stops without modifying any file and reports the record as not yet actionable — this is not a normal "build failed" outcome, it is the record's own documented gate.
2. `permittedGrants` (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`) returns only the per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` shape — no flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys at the top level.

## Current State
Three functions in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` carry the same directory-staleness stanza: `let mtimeMs; try { mtimeMs = fs.statSync(dir).mtimeMs; } catch { return false; } return (now - mtimeMs) > TTL;` — `isAdHocStandaloneSuperseded` against `ADHOC_SUPERSEDED_TTL_MS` (30d), `isOrphanedMint` against `ORPHAN_MINT_TTL_MS` (24h), and `isStructurallyStuck` against `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_TTL_MS` (7d). Each takes `now = Date.now()` as its last parameter and treats an unstat-able directory as not stale (fail toward "keep"). The copies are byte-for-byte the same logic, so a change to the staleness basis (ctime instead of mtime, tolerating clock skew, treating `ENOENT` differently from `EACCES`) has to be made three times, and `isAbandonedInterrupted`, which uses the events log rather than the stat, is the reminder that a fourth copy would be the path of least resistance for the next detector. The related consolidation records (#1732 classifier, #1733 loop extraction) both build on this primitive existing first.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `isStaleDir(dir, ttlMs, now = Date.now())` in `archive-merged.js`: the one stat-and-compare, returning `false` on any stat failure, `true` iff `(now - mtimeMs) > ttlMs`; exported alongside the existing predicates.
- [ ] `isAdHocStandaloneSuperseded`, `isOrphanedMint`, and `isStructurallyStuck` each reduce to their own guard clauses plus one `isStaleDir(dir, <their constant>, now)` call; their signatures, exports, and `now` defaults unchanged.
- [ ] Unit tests for the primitive in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` beside the existing `fs.utimesSync`-backdated fixtures: stale past TTL → `true`; exactly at TTL → `false` (strict `>` preserved); fresh → `false`; missing directory → `false`.
- [ ] The three predicates' existing cases stay green unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `archive-merged.js` contains exactly one `fs.statSync(...).mtimeMs` expression, inside `isStaleDir`.
2. The three predicates call `isStaleDir` with their own TTL constant; the constants' names and values are unchanged and still exported.
3. `isStaleDir` is exported and has its own test cases for the four outcomes above, including the boundary (`now - mtimeMs === ttlMs` is not stale).
4. All existing cases in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` pass without modification; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
A mechanical extraction: the stanza's only free variables are `dir`, the TTL constant, and `now`. Keep the comparison strict (`>`) and the catch-to-`false` posture identical; both are load-bearing (`isStructurallyStuck`'s comment: "pure except for the one mtime stat", and the orphan-mint comment's fail-toward-keep rationale). Land first among the four `archive-merged.js` records: #1732's classifier calls this helper, and #1733/#1737 are independent of it but touch the same file, so sequence, never parallel.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `isAdHocStandaloneSuperseded`, `isOrphanedMint`, `isStructurallyStuck`, `module.exports`.
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — backdated-`utimesSync` fixtures for the orphan-mint and structurally-stuck cases are the template.

## Gotchas
- Other `statSync(...).mtimeMs` sites in the plugin (`file-lock.js`'s lock age, `residue/probes/artifacts.js`'s basis, `visual-decide/server.js`'s signature) compare against different things or for different purposes; they are out of scope and must not be routed through this helper.
- `isAbandonedInterrupted` is not a stat-based detector (events-log recency); do not force it onto `isStaleDir`.
- Do not change the fail-closed direction: an unreadable directory is "not stale" everywhere today, and `archiveMerged()` relies on that to leave a permission-broken run dir alone.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`agent-browser` is a third-party tool this plugin depends on optionally (CLAUDE.md's Dependencies
table) — it is not part of this repo's own codebase; `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md`
documents its usage but does not own its implementation. That reference file's documented operation
vocabulary (open, snapshot, find, click, fill, screenshot, vitals, trace, etc.) has no
color-scheme/emulation flag.

Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by
`prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML
fixture with the target CSS rules copied in and the desired scheme's token values inlined, opened
via `file://`, instead of driving the live app in the actual scheme under test — a real but
indirect substitute.

Because `agent-browser` is external, this record's scope is bounded by what this repo can
actually change: whether the tool already supports color-scheme emulation through some mechanism
not yet documented here, and if not, formalizing the documented workaround so a future verifier
doesn't have to rediscover it.

## Deliverables

- Investigate whether the installed `agent-browser` version already supports color-scheme
  emulation via an undocumented flag, environment variable, or underlying CDP passthrough (e.g.
  `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`) — check its own `--help` output and any bundled documentation
  first.
- If a mechanism already exists: document it in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s operation
  vocabulary, with a usage example.
- If no mechanism exists: document the standalone-HTML-fixture workaround (build a minimal
  fixture with the target CSS and the desired scheme's token values inlined, open via `file://`)
  as the recommended pattern in `agent-browser-reference.md`, so a future verifier facing the same
  gap has a documented path instead of reinventing it — and, separately, file feedback against
  `agent-browser` itself (outside this repo) requesting the capability, since this repo cannot add
  a feature to a tool it doesn't own.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `agent-browser-reference.md` documents either (a) a working color-scheme emulation flag/option,
  verified against the actually-installed tool version, or (b) the standalone-fixture workaround
  pattern, clearly labeled as a workaround rather than a native capability.
- Whichever path is documented is validated by actually using it to verify a light-mode-only (or
  dark-mode-only) CSS change against a real project with `prefers-color-scheme`-only theming —
  not merely described in the abstract.
- If no native mechanism exists, upstream feedback is filed against `agent-browser` (outside this
  repo's own issue tracker) requesting the capability, and that filing is referenced from this
  record's closing comment.

## Technical Approach

Run `agent-browser --help` (and any subcommand-specific help, e.g. `agent-browser open --help`)
against the actually-installed version to check for an existing but undocumented emulation
option before assuming none exists — third-party tools frequently expose CDP-passthrough flags
that aren't surfaced in every doc surface. If nothing surfaces, formalize the fixture-based
workaround already used as a real substitute: a minimal standalone HTML file with the target
CSS rules and the desired scheme's computed token values inlined, opened via `agent-browser open
file://<path>`. Document whichever path is real in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s existing
operation-vocabulary section, in the same format as its other documented operations.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md` — document the flag (if found) or the
  fixture-workaround pattern (if not)

## Gotchas

- `agent-browser` is a third-party dependency, not part of this repo's own codebase — this
  record cannot add a capability to the tool itself; it can only document what already exists or
  formalize a workaround, plus file upstream feedback if the capability is genuinely absent.
- Don't document a workaround as if it were a native capability — the Acceptance Criteria
  requires the documentation to be honest about which case applies.

## Original request

**Summary:** Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by `prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML fixture instead of driving the live app, because agent-browser's documented operation vocabulary has no color-scheme/emulation flag.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** skills/browse (agent-browser-reference.md)

**Use case:** A project ships theming entirely via `prefers-color-scheme` with no manual toggle in the UI. Verifying a change scoped to the non-default color scheme (e.g. light mode when the OS/browser default is dark) requires driving the app in that scheme. `agent-browser`'s documented operation vocabulary (open, snapshot, find, click, fill, screenshot, vitals, trace, etc. per agent-browser-reference.md) has no color-scheme emulation option, so the only available workaround is building a standalone HTML fixture with the target CSS rules copied in and the desired scheme's token values inlined, then opening it via `file://` — a real but indirect substitute for driving the live app in the actual scheme under test.

**Definition:** Clear

Surface: infra

## Current State

`fileMatchesFrontendPredicate` (`plugin/bin/lib/design-detect/index.js`, the Layer 3 sniff) returns true when a file's extension is in `TRIGGER_EXTENSIONS` or when any path segment is in `TRIGGER_PATH_SEGMENTS = ['components', 'pages', 'app', 'routes', 'views', 'ui']`. The segment rule exists so app-router `page.ts`/`layout.ts` files without a rendering extension are still caught. It has no exclusion, so Next.js API route handlers — `app/api/**/route.{ts,js}` (app router) and `pages/api/**` (pages router) — match on the `app`/`pages` segment even though they render nothing. `skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md`'s Match rule (two positive clauses, no exclusion) and its Negative cases list (which names `.ts`/`.js` "outside any trigger path" only) describe the same behavior, so the sniff and its documentation agree with each other and are both wrong for this case.

Observed on plugin 6.114.0: a record whose diff was two `app/api/**/route.ts` handlers, one vitest file, and four markdown files, with no `Surface:` header (filed before that field existed, so Layer 2 could not rule), returned `{"decision":"proceed","track":"web"}` from `design-detect.js` in `review`, `polish`, and `survey` modes. The run overrode the verdict by hand three times, each logged as a deviation, while `/build`'s own design pre-build step on the same run had already been skipped as "no frontend surface". Layer 3 is a fallback that runs only when nothing was declared (`layer3Applies`), so the false positive costs exactly the records that most need the sniff to be right.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js` (245 lines) covers "trigger path segments match regardless of extension" and the zero-match skip; no case exercises an API route path.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add an API-route exclusion to `fileMatchesFrontendPredicate`: after the extension check (a `.tsx` under `app/api/` still matches on extension) and before the segment scan, return false when the normalized path contains `app/api/` or `pages/api/` as adjacent segments (`(^|/)(app|pages)/api/`), so the `app`/`pages` segment rule never fires for a Next.js API route. Keep `TRIGGER_PATH_SEGMENTS` unchanged; the exclusion is a named constant (`API_ROUTE_SEGMENTS` or a regex) with a comment citing this record and the two Next.js conventions.
- [ ] `frontend-detection.md`: add a third clause to the Match rule stating the exclusion (segment matches under `app/api/` or `pages/api/` do not count; extension matches still do), and add "Next.js API route handlers — `app/api/**/route.{ts,js}`, `pages/api/**`" to the Negative cases list, so the sniff and its documentation agree.
- [ ] `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js`: `app/api/users/route.ts` and `pages/api/health.ts` do not match; `src/app/api/x/route.js` does not match; `app/api/x/page.tsx` still matches (extension wins); `app/dashboard/page.ts` still matches (segment rule intact); `layer3` over the observed file list (two `app/api/**/route.ts`, one `.test.ts`, four `.md`) returns the sniff skip.
- [ ] `docs/incident-log.md` / `CLAUDE.md` untouched; if `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `design-detect` line enumerates the trigger tables, leave it — the tables themselves did not change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `fileMatchesFrontendPredicate('app/api/users/route.ts')`, `('pages/api/health.ts')`, and `('src/app/api/x/route.js')` return false; `('app/api/x/page.tsx')` and `('app/dashboard/page.ts')` return true.
2. `layer3([...two app/api route.ts, one .test.ts, four .md])` returns `{ proceed: false, reason: SKIP_REASONS.NON_FRONTEND_SNIFF }`; `node bin/design-detect.js --mode review` over the same list returns a skip decision, not `proceed`.
3. Every existing case in `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js` and `cli.test.js` passes unchanged.
4. `frontend-detection.md`'s Match rule has the exclusion clause and its Negative cases list names Next.js API route handlers with both path shapes.
5. `npm test` green.

## Technical Approach

One predicate change, no new layer: the exclusion is scoped to the two Next.js API conventions the report observed, applied only to the segment rule so the extension rule keeps precedence. Do not generalise to `routes/` (SvelteKit `+server.ts`, Remix resource routes) in this record — those are a different convention with a different marker and belong in a follow-up if observed; name that boundary in the code comment.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/design-detect/index.js` — exclusion constant + check in `fileMatchesFrontendPredicate`, above the segment scan
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md` — Match rule clause 3; Negative cases bullet
- `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js` — the cases in Deliverables

## Gotchas

- Normalize backslashes before matching (the function already does); the exclusion regex must run on the normalized string so Windows paths behave.
- `pages/api/` under a `src/` prefix and `app/api/` nested inside a monorepo package path (`packages/web/app/api/...`) must both be excluded; anchor on the adjacent segment pair, not on path start.
- A `.tsx` under `app/api/` is exotic but possible (a handler that renders an OG image with JSX); the extension rule keeps it frontend on purpose, and the test pins that.
- `frontend-detection.md`'s trigger tables are cited as "web-only" by the native track's routing paragraph; the exclusion does not change that property, so no native-track text needs editing.

## Original request

**Summary:** `design-detect.js`'s Layer 3 path sniff marks Next.js app-router API route handlers (`app/api/**/route.ts`) as frontend, so a backend-only record without a `Surface:` header returns `proceed` for review, polish and survey.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** bin/lib/design-detect (Layer 3 file-extension / path-segment sniff) and skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md

**Use case:**
Layer 3's trigger-path table treats any file under a `/app/` segment as frontend so that app-router `page.ts`/`layout.ts` files without a `.tsx` extension are still caught. That rule also matches `app/api/**/route.ts` — Next.js app-router API route handlers, which render nothing. On a record whose diff was two Next.js API route handler files (`app/api/**/route.ts`) plus a vitest file and four markdown files, with no `Surface:` header (a code-health-filed record predating that field), `design-detect.js --mode review`, `--mode polish` and `--mode survey` all returned `{"decision":"proceed","track":"web"}`. The caller then either pays for Impeccable critique/audit over request handlers, or overrides the CLI's verdict by hand — which is what the run did, three times, each as a logged deviation — while `/build`'s own design pre-build step on the same run had already been skipped for "no frontend surface, two backend API route files".

Suggested change: exclude `**/app/api/**/route.{ts,js}` (and `pages/api/**`) from the `/app/` and `/pages/` path triggers, or require a rendering extension when the only match is a path segment and the file is a `route.ts`; add "Next.js API route handlers" to `frontend-detection.md`'s Negative cases list so the sniff and its documentation agree.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s by-number escape hatch (lines ~1295-1314) exists
to unstick a run whose worktree and branch are both gone (`#1962`): it re-resolves the run's PR
directly by `state.pr.number` via `resolvePrStateByNumber`, and archives immediately **only when
`byNumber.state === 'CLOSED'`** (an unmerged close has nothing to catch up on). There is no
branch at all for `byNumber.state === 'MERGED'` — the most common real-world case, since GitHub
auto-deletes a branch after merge and a worktree is routinely reaped after that. A merged-but-
unhandled run falls straight through to the plain `no-branch` skip, which after
`STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_TTL_MS` (7 days) of no further mtime activity gets classified
`isStructurallyStuck()` and escalated by `escalate-residue.js` into a GitHub issue titled
`reconcile: structurally-stuck stuck on {path}` (see #644) — permanently, since nothing in the
sweep ever revisits a `no-branch` skip once escalated.

Confirmed against the currently-open instances of this exact escalation: `#2225` (this record,
path `.../2026-09-01T125854-record-1452`, PR #1763 MERGED 2026-09-01), plus nine more open
issues whose referenced run dirs each stamp a `state.pr.number` for a PR that has since merged —
`#2226` (PR #1761), `#2228` (PR #1760), `#2229` (PR #1759), `#2354` (PR #1901), `#2355` (PR
#1850), `#2356` (PR #1842), `#2357` (PR #1525), `#2358` (PR #1907), `#2359` (PR #1891) — all
confirmed `MERGED` via `gh pr view {n} --json state,mergedAt`. Ten separate, independently-filed
GitHub issues are symptoms of this one code gap, not ten unrelated problems.

(Two further open issues in this same title family — `#2230` and `#2231` — reference PRs that
are `CLOSED` but unmerged (#1509, #1497). Those already match the *existing* CLOSED branch's
condition, so they are a different, still-open question (their run dirs have no `console.json`
at all, so `readConsoleState` reads `'none'`/`console-never-rendered`, which the CLOSED branch
also currently skips on) — **out of scope for this record**; tracked separately, not fixed here.)

## Deliverables

- Add a `byNumber.state === 'MERGED'` branch to the by-number escape hatch in
  `archive-merged.js`, mirroring the existing branch-based merged-PR path immediately below it
  (`resolvePrState` → `decideArchive` → `localHasMerge` → `archiveRunDir`): gate on the same
  `readConsoleState`/`decideArchive` resolved-console check the CLOSED branch already applies,
  then run the identical `localHasMerge(root, byNumber.mergeCommit)` fast-forward check the
  branch-based merged path uses before calling `archiveRunDir`, using `byNumber.mergeCommit` in
  place of `prState.mergeCommit` (the by-number lookup carries the same field — verify this
  against `pr-state.js`'s `resolvePrStateByNumber` return shape before wiring it in).
- Add a test case to `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`, alongside the existing
  by-number `CLOSED`/`OPEN` cases (~line 1723), covering `byNumber.state === 'MERGED'` with a
  local fast-forward past the merge commit — asserting the run archives.
- Once this fix ships and the next reconcile sweep runs against the live repo, verify it clears
  the ten currently-escalated `no-branch` issues named in Current State (or as many as still have
  their run dir present — some may since have been manually archived).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `archiveMerged()` archives a run whose worktree and branch are both gone, whose
  `state.pr.number` resolves (via `resolvePrStateByNumber`) to a `MERGED` PR, and whose local
  checkout is fast-forward of that PR's merge commit — the identical outcome the existing
  branch-based merged-PR path already produces for a run that still has a resolvable branch.
- The same run is still skipped (not archived) when `localHasMerge` returns `false` (local
  checkout behind the merge commit) or `undefined` (merge commit unknown) — the by-number MERGED
  branch must not skip this safety check just because it takes a different code path to get
  there.
- The existing by-number `CLOSED` and `OPEN` behaviors (archive immediately / fall through to
  `no-branch` skip, respectively) are unchanged — this is a strict addition, not a rewrite of the
  existing branch.
- The new test in `archive-merged.test.js` fails if the `MERGED` branch is removed, proving it
  actually exercises the new code path.
- `#2230` and `#2231` (the CLOSED-but-console-never-rendered case) are explicitly out of scope —
  this record's fix must not attempt to also resolve those two.

## Technical Approach

In `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`, inside the `if (stampedWorktree && state &&
state.pr && state.pr.number)` block (~line 1295), add a sibling branch to the existing
`if (byNumber && ... byNumber.state === 'CLOSED')` check:

```js
if (byNumber && typeof byNumber === 'object' && byNumber.state === 'MERGED') {
  const consoleState = readConsoleState(dir);
  const decision = decideArchive(byNumber, consoleState);
  if (decision.action === 'skip') {
    skipped.push({ runDir: dir, reason: decision.reason });
    continue;
  }
  const hasMerge = localHasMerge(root, byNumber.mergeCommit);
  if (hasMerge !== true) {
    skipped.push({ runDir: dir, reason: hasMerge === false ? 'local-behind-merge' : 'merge-commit-unknown' });
    continue;
  }
  if (dryRun) { archived.push(dir); continue; }
  const result = archiveRunDir(root, dir);
  trackArchiveResult(root, repoSlug, dir, result);
  if (!result.ok) { skipped.push({ runDir: dir, reason: result.reason }); continue; }
  archived.push(dir);
  continue;
}
```

Verify `resolvePrStateByNumber`'s actual return shape (`pr-state.js`) carries `mergeCommit` under
the same field name `resolvePrState` does before wiring this in — this snippet assumes parity but
that assumption needs a one-line confirmation against the real implementation, not a rewrite of
`pr-state.js` itself. `decideArchive`'s own signature already accepts a `prState`-shaped object
generically (it's already called with both `resolvePrState`'s and the by-number lookup's outputs
elsewhere in this same file for the CLOSED case's sibling logic), so reusing it here should not
require changing its signature.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — add the `MERGED` branch to the by-number escape
  hatch (~line 1295-1314)
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js` — read-only reference: confirm `resolvePrStateByNumber`'s
  return shape carries `mergeCommit`
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — add the `MERGED` case test (~near line 1723,
  alongside the existing `CLOSED`/`OPEN` by-number tests)

## Gotchas

- Ten currently-open GitHub issues (`#2226`, `#2228`, `#2229`, `#2354`, `#2355`, `#2356`, `#2357`,
  `#2358`, `#2359`, plus this record `#2225`) are symptoms of this exact gap, confirmed by
  checking each referenced PR's merge state directly — they are not being independently shaped
  into their own build specs by this sweep, to avoid ten redundant PRs fixing the identical
  one-function gap. Once this fix merges, close the other nine as duplicates (referencing this
  record) once reconcile's next sweep confirms their run dirs actually archive — do not close
  them pre-emptively before that confirmation, since a run dir that still doesn't archive after
  this fix ships means the gap wasn't fully understood and those issues should stay open.
- `#2230`/`#2231` are a different, still-open sub-problem (CLOSED-unmerged PRs whose run dirs
  never got a `console.json` at all) — do not fold a fix for that into this record; it needs its
  own diagnosis of why `console-never-rendered` isn't itself eligible for archival.
- This fix only prevents *future* silent accumulation and lets already-escalated instances heal
  on the next reconcile sweep — it does not retroactively touch the GitHub issues themselves;
  closing them is a separate, manual (or tidy-driven) step once the sweep confirms each path
  actually cleared.

## Original request
